pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.explain: A folder (not a ROS package itself) holding two small, heavily commented template packages to COPY when you want to replace or add a piece of the simulation: example_detector (detector slot) and example_listener (extras slot). Both are built by simulation/setup/03_build.sh like every other package. Each template README follows the same five steps: copy -> rename -> change -> plug in with a profile -> check with 'ros2 run sim_plugins check_slot'. Status per AGENTS.md: WIP templates.
pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.how_it_fits: They are the hands-on side of sim_plugins: simulation/profiles/example_detector.yaml and example_listener.yaml plug them in ('bash simulation/scripts/demo.sh --profile example_detector'), and the slot rules they follow are the contracts in docs/simulation/PLUGINS.md.

pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.explain: A template detector you copy to make your own. On the outside it does EXACTLY what the team's detection/new_od does, so main_controller and the demo panel use it unchanged: it watches the team photo folder <ros2_ws>/src/video_cam/mapping_photos for new '<lat> , <lon>.jpg' photos, finds the hiker (class '0') and the tent (class '1') - here simply by colour - and publishes ONE interfaces/ImageResult per photo on /image_detection (RELIABLE, depth 10), even when nothing is found. It also answers /sahi/get_health with 'ModelLoaded: True'.
pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.how_it_fits: Replaces new_od in the simulator through the profile simulation/profiles/example_detector.yaml (detector.kind custom): team_stack.launch.py then includes a copy of tracker.launch.xml without new_od (tracker_filter.py) and starts launch/example_detector.launch.py instead; demo.sh waits for node 'example_detector'. Input: photo files written by video_cam (which got them from the camera emulator). Output: /image_detection to main_controller. Optional input: /mavros/mission/reached (copied into waypoint_index). Check: 'ros2 run sim_plugins check_slot --slot detector --take-photo'.

pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.explain: A template 'extra' you copy to make your own logger or monitor. It only LISTENS to the flight - MAVROS telemetry, mission progress, shutter presses, the detector's results and the text messages - and logs a running summary every 10 s; when it stops it saves the summary as JSON (~/.astra_sim/example_listener_summary.json). It publishes nothing, so it can never disturb the mission (the rule for extras).
pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.how_it_fits: Plugged in through a profile's extras list (simulation/profiles/example_listener.yaml), started with the team stack (start_with team_stack) by team_stack.launch.py through launch_support.entry_actions. Subscribes /mavros/state, /mavros/global_position/global, /mavros/global_position/rel_alt, /mavros/mission/reached, /mavros/statustext/recv (from MAVROS), /camera/trigger (the team's shutter) and /image_detection (from the detector). Check: 'ros2 run sim_plugins check_slot --slot extras --node example_listener'.

pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins.explain: The 'plug and play' part of the simulator. It lets a teammate swap ONE piece of the simulation for their own - the autopilot (any ArduCopter SITL version, a source build, or an autopilot on another computer), the camera, the detector, the mission brain, the world, extra programs, or the whole team stack (another checkout of the Jetson code, run.team_repo) - by writing a small YAML 'profile' that only lists what differs from the default. It checks the profile, turns it into launch arguments and script variables, and has check_slot, which looks at the live ROS graph to prove the new piece talks exactly like the one it replaces. Status per AGENTS.md: WIP (unit-tested; custom detectors and alternate SITL still need recorded runs).
pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins.how_it_fits: Used by simulation/scripts/demo.sh and start_sim.sh (through 'profile_tool shell'), and by sim_bringup's sim.launch.py and team_stack.launch.py (through launch_support.py and tracker_filter.py) when a profile:= / --profile option is given; with no profile option nothing here is even imported, so the simulator runs exactly as before. Profiles live in simulation/profiles/*.yaml; the slot contracts (topics such as /image_detection, /mavros/*, the camera at 192.168.144.25 UDP 37260 + HTTP 82) are written in contracts.py and copied into docs/simulation/PLUGINS.md by doc_blocks.py. Commands: 'ros2 run sim_plugins profile_tool ...', 'check_slot --slot ...', 'model_check' (a detector weights file) and 'run_meta' (records which pieces really ran).

pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: A pretend SIYI gimbal camera for the simulator. On the real drone a SIYI camera (ZR10 or A8 mini) sits at 192.168.144.25; the team's video_cam driver points it with SIYI SDK commands on UDP port 37260 and downloads each photo from its web server on TCP port 82. This package answers on the same address and ports with the same bytes, but moves a gimbal and takes the photos inside Gazebo, so video_cam runs unchanged with its default settings and gets real rendered pictures.
pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: It sits between the team stack and Gazebo. Team side: video_cam (ROS node 'siyi') sends SDK frames to 192.168.144.25:37260 (a loopback alias on this PC, added by simulation/setup/camera_ip_alias.sh or scripts/add_camera_ip.sh) and polls/downloads photos over HTTP port 82; each photo becomes '<lat> , <lon>.jpg' in mapping_photos for the detector. Gazebo side (gz-transport, no ROS bridge): gimbal joint targets on /sim/gimbal/yaw|roll|pitch/cmd_pos, the photo trigger /sim/camera/photo/trigger, and inputs /sim/gimbal/joint_states, /sim/drone/odometry and /sim/camera/photo/image from the iris_a8mini drone model (sim_models). ROS extras: /sim/camera/photo_info (one JSON per photo, read by sim_demo's score_run, demo_markers and truth_detector) and /sim/camera/emulator_state (2 Hz health). sim_bringup's sim.launch.py starts node 'siyi_emulator' with config/siyi_emulator.yaml plus camera_model, camera_ip, sd_card_dir ~/.astra_sim/sd_card_I<instance> and, from camera_max_zoom, max_zoom (demo.sh uses 1 = '--zoom survey'). The sim_plugins camera slot checks it with siyi_probe.py.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.explain: Overview of the two templates: example_detector (reads the team's photos like new_od and publishes interfaces/ImageResult on /image_detection, here with a colour-blob rule) and example_listener (logs telemetry, mission progress, shutter presses and detections), how to try each with demo.sh --profile, and the shared five steps copy -> rename -> change -> plug in -> check.

Guide to the template detector: what it does on the outside (same as new_od), its files, the five steps with exact commands and the table of names to rename, the profile to write, how to run it by hand with parameters (camera_feed_path, min_blob_area_px, HSV colour ranges), and a troubleshooting table (main_controller waiting 90 s, drops aimed at the photo centre, 'STAND-IN' banner, BEST_EFFORT QoS, missing node_name, missing interfaces).
Marks the folder as the Python package example_detector and says in its purpose text what blob_logic and node do and how to start, demo and check it.

The 'brain' of the template detector, with no ROS so it can be tested with plain pytest and swapped for your own model without touching node.py. It finds the hiker and the tent by COLOUR: every connected patch of pixels whose HSV colour is in a class's range (placeholders: person orange/yellow, tent blue) and whose size is plausible becomes one Detection, with class_id '0' person / '1' tent, a score 0..1 and the box centre and size in FULL-photo pixels (what main_controller needs to aim).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.how_it_fits: Called by node.py for every new photo; also holds the photo-name helpers (is_photo, latlon_from_name) that match how the team's video_cam names files.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_exa.explain: One found object in FULL-photo pixels: class_id ('0' person, '1' tent), score 0..1, box centre cx, cy (from the left and top edges) and box width w and height h.
Property: the box area in pixels (w x h).
Property: the class name, 'person' or 'tent' ('object' for anything else).

True for a finished photo file: it ends in .jpg, .jpeg or .png, does not contain '.tmp.' (video_cam writes '<name>.tmp.jpg' first and then renames it) and does not start with a dot. Sidecar .json files are not photos.

Reads the GPS position from a team photo name: '36.215026 , -96.006800.jpg' (space, comma, space) -> (36.215026, -96.0068). Names without a position (like 'IMG_0001.jpg') or with impossible numbers give (0.0, 0.0), which main_controller ignores.

Finds connected patches of one colour range in an OpenCV picture: converts to HSV, keeps pixels inside [low, high], removes single noisy pixels (a 3x3 'opening'), labels the connected patches and keeps those whose pixel count is between min_area and max_area. Returns (cx, cy, w, h, fill) per patch, where fill = coloured pixels / box area.

Finds persons and tents in one photo: works on a 1/4-size copy for speed (downscale 4), runs find_blobs for each class's colour range with the size limits scaled to that copy, scores each patch 0.5 + 0.5 x fill (max 1.0), scales the boxes back to FULL-photo pixels, and keeps at most 5 per class (best score first). This is the function to replace with your own model.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.explain: The ROS 2 node of the template detector ('example_detector'). Every scan_period_s (1 s) it looks in the team photo folder for new finished photos, runs blob_logic.detect on each, and publishes ONE interfaces/ImageResult per photo on /image_detection (RELIABLE, depth 10) filled exactly like new_od fills it; it answers /sahi/get_health like new_od so demo.sh can wait for it. Parameters: camera_feed_path, scan_period_s, process_existing, min/max_blob_area_px, downscale, person/tent_hsv_low/high, serve_health, method_name.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.how_it_fits: Reads the photos video_cam saves (from the camera emulator in the simulator); main_controller subscribes to /image_detection and waits until every photo name has been reported. Subscribes /mavros/mission/reached (if mavros_msgs is installed) to fill waypoint_index.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_exa.explain: Finds the team photo folder the way video_cam and new_od do: walks up from this file (at most 10 levels) to the folder that has both install/ and src/ (the ros2_ws) and returns <ros2_ws>/src/video_cam/mapping_photos; falls back to ~/ODLC_Machine_Inferencing_System_2025-2026/ros2_ws/src/video_cam/mapping_photos.
The template detector node: photo folder in, /image_detection out.

Creates node 'example_detector': declares the parameters, picks the folder (camera_feed_path or the team folder, created if missing), creates the RELIABLE depth-10 /image_detection publisher (a BEST_EFFORT one would never reach main_controller), subscribes /mavros/mission/reached if possible, serves /sahi/get_health if serve_health, optionally marks photos already present as seen, and starts the scan timer.
Remembers the mission item just reached (wp_seq from /mavros/mission/reached), later copied into ImageResult.waypoint_index.

Answers /sahi/get_health in new_od's format: success true and 'Healthy: True, ConsecErrors: <errors>, ModelLoaded: True, Format: colour-blobs' (stack_check --need-detector looks for 'ModelLoaded: True').

Timer callback: lists new finished photos in the folder (oldest first by modification time) and processes each exactly once. A photo counts as finished when its size has not changed since the last scan and it is at least 0.3 s old (a safety net; video_cam writes atomically).

Reads one photo with OpenCV, runs blob_logic.detect (an unreadable photo counts an error and gets an EMPTY result, so main_controller still sees its name), publishes the ImageResult on /image_detection and logs what was found.

Builds one ImageResult exactly like new_od: header frame 'camera', a vision_msgs Detection2DArray with one Detection2D per object (class_id, score, box centre and size in full-photo pixels), image_name = the file name only, ISO timestamp, num_detections, method, waypoint_index, latitude/longitude from the file name, and the parallel lists classes, confidences, areas and descriptions.
Entry point of 'ros2 run example_detector example_detector': starts ROS, creates the ExampleDetector node and spins it until Ctrl+C or the launch system stops it, then shuts down cleanly.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.explain: Launch file that starts the template detector node (named 'example_detector', the node_name the profile gives) with its settings as launch arguments a profile can set through detector.custom.args: min_blob_area_px (150), camera_feed_path ('' = the team folder), scan_period_s (1.0) and serve_health (true).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.how_it_fits: Included by team_stack.launch.py (through launch_support.entry_actions) when simulation/profiles/example_detector.yaml is used.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_exa.explain: Declares the four launch arguments and the Node package example_detector / executable example_detector / name example_detector, converting each launch-argument text into the right parameter type (int, str, float, bool) with ParameterValue.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_exa.called_when: ros2 launch example_detector example_detector.launch.py, or team_stack.launch.py with the example_detector profile

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.explain: Manifest of the template detector (example_detector 0.1.0, ament_python, MIT, maintainer astra-sim@example.com). Run-time needs: rclpy, launch, launch_ros, the team's interfaces (ImageResult), vision_msgs, std_srvs, mavros_msgs, OpenCV and numpy; pytest for tests.
Empty marker file that registers the package name example_detector in the ament index (rename it when you copy the template).
Tells setuptools to install the example_detector command in lib/example_detector, where 'ros2 run' looks for it.

Build recipe of the template detector: installs the Python module, launch/example_detector.launch.py (so a profile can say 'launch: example_detector.launch.py') and the README, and creates the command 'ros2 run example_detector example_detector' (example_detector.node:main). When copying, rename package_name, the folders and the entry point.

Unit tests of blob_logic.py without ROS: the photo-name rules the team's video_cam uses (temporary .tmp. files, sidecars and hidden files are not photos; '<lat> , <lon>' names give the position) and that colour blobs come back as person/tent boxes in FULL-photo pixels with sane scores.

Guide to the template extra: an example of the summary it logs, its files, the topics it listens to and why /mavros/* use BEST_EFFORT QoS, the five steps copy -> rename -> change -> plug in (a profile extras entry with package, executable, node_name, start_with, args) -> check, and a small troubleshooting table.
Marks the folder as the Python package example_listener and says in its purpose text what summary.py and node.py do and how to start, demo and check it.

The ROS 2 node of the template extra ('example_listener'). It subscribes to seven topics, feeds every message into a FlightSummary, logs the summary every summary_period_s (10 s; 0 = only at the end) and saves it as JSON to summary_file ('' = $ASTRA_SIM_HOME or ~/.astra_sim/example_listener_summary.json) when it stops. MAVROS topics and /camera/trigger use BEST_EFFORT QoS (hears every publisher); /image_detection uses RELIABLE like main_controller.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.effects: subscribes topic:/mavros/state, topic:/mavros/global_position/global, topic:/mavros/global_position/rel_alt, topic:/mavros/mission/reached, topic:/mavros/statustext/recv, topic:/camera/trigger, topic:/image_detection; writes the summary JSON at exit
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.how_it_fits: Listens to MAVROS (/mavros/state, /mavros/global_position/global, /mavros/global_position/rel_alt, /mavros/mission/reached, /mavros/statustext/recv), the team's shutter /camera/trigger and the detector's /image_detection. Publishes nothing.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_exa.explain: The template listener node: every message goes into a FlightSummary that is printed and saved.

Creates node 'example_listener': reads summary_period_s and summary_file, creates the FlightSummary, subscribes the six MAVROS/shutter topics with BEST_EFFORT QoS (small lambdas pass the right fields to on_state, on_fix, on_rel_alt, on_reached, on_statustext, on_trigger) and /image_detection with RELIABLE depth 10, and starts the print timer.
Turns one ImageResult from /image_detection into (class_id, score) pairs from each detection's results[0] and passes them with the photo name to FlightSummary.on_detection.
Timer callback: logs 'summary:' followed by the FlightSummary text.
Writes the summary as indented JSON to summary_file (creating its folder); a write error is only logged as a warning.
Entry point of 'ros2 run example_listener example_listener': starts ROS, spins the ExampleListener until Ctrl+C or the launch system stops it, then saves the summary and shuts down cleanly.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.explain: The bookkeeping of the template listener, free of ROS so it is easy to test and change. Fed one message at a time as plain values, it keeps a running summary: flight (modes seen, armed time, highest altitude above home, distance flown from GPS fixes), mission (items reached in order), camera (shutter presses), detections (photos reported, detections per class, best confidence per class and its photo) and the last 5 STATUSTEXT lines.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.how_it_fits: node.py feeds it from the ROS topics; text() is what the node prints every few seconds, as_dict() what it saves as JSON.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_exa.explain: Great-circle distance in metres between two GPS positions using the haversine formula with an Earth radius of 6,371,000 m (0.001 deg of latitude is about 111 m).

The running summary of one flight: connected/armed flags, modes seen, armed time, maximum height above home, distance flown, last GPS fix, mission items reached, shutter presses, photos reported, detections per class, best score per class with its photo, and the last 5 text messages.
Takes a mavros_msgs/State: stores 'connected', adds the flight mode when it changes, and starts or stops the armed-time clock when the drone arms or disarms.
Takes a GPS fix (latitude, longitude): ignores impossible positions and (0, 0), adds the distance from the previous fix to the total (jumps of 200 m or more are ignored) and remembers this fix.
Takes the height above home from /mavros/global_position/rel_alt and keeps the highest value seen (non-finite values are ignored).
Adds the number of the mission item just reached (wp_seq) to the list.
Counts one shutter press for each true message on /camera/trigger.
Keeps the last 5 non-empty STATUSTEXT lines (from /mavros/statustext/recv).

Takes one photo's detection results [(class_id, score)]: counts the photo, counts each detection under 'person', 'tent' or 'object', and remembers the best score per class with the photo it came from.
Returns the total armed time so far, including the current armed period if the drone is armed now.

Makes the five readable summary lines the node logs: flight (connected, armed, modes, armed seconds, max height, distance), mission (last 12 items reached), camera (shutter presses), detections (photos reported, counts, best per class) and messages.
Returns everything as plain JSON-friendly values (rounded times, height and distance, lists, counts, best score and image per class, last messages) for the JSON file.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.explain: Manifest of the template extra (example_listener 0.1.0, ament_python, MIT, maintainer astra-sim@example.com). Run-time needs: rclpy, the team's interfaces, mavros_msgs, sensor_msgs and std_msgs; pytest for tests.
Empty marker file that registers the package name example_listener in the ament index (rename it when you copy the template).
Tells setuptools to install the example_listener command in lib/example_listener, where 'ros2 run' looks for it.

Build recipe of the template extra: installs the Python module and README and creates the command 'ros2 run example_listener example_listener' (example_listener.node:main). When copying, rename package_name, the folders and the entry point.
Unit tests of summary.py without ROS: the haversine distance (0.001 deg latitude is about 111 m), armed time, modes, distance flown, best detection per class, and the JSON summary.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/R.explain: Guide for people who change sim_plugins itself: every profile_tool and check_slot command, what each module does and whether it needs ROS, the rule that only non-default settings produce arguments (so no profile = today's behaviour), how to regenerate the PLUGINS.md tables after changing schema.py or contracts.py, and how to run the tests. The user guide is docs/simulation/PLUGINS.md.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/p.explain: ROS 2 package manifest of sim_plugins (version 0.1.0, ament_python, MIT, maintainer astra-sim@example.com). It needs PyYAML for profiles, rclpy only for check_slot, the launch libraries only for launch_support, plus std_msgs, std_srvs and rcl_interfaces. The team's interfaces, mavros_msgs and nav_msgs are imported lazily by check_slot and deliberately not listed, so this package builds even when the team packages do not.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/r.explain: An empty marker file that registers the package name sim_plugins in the ament index so ROS 2 tools can find it.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: Tells setuptools to install the two commands in lib/sim_plugins, where 'ros2 run sim_plugins ...' looks for them.

Build and install recipe: installs the sim_plugins Python modules and README and creates four commands: 'profile_tool' (sim_plugins.profile_tool:main: list, validate, plan, resolve, contract, shell, docs), 'check_slot' (sim_plugins.check_slot:main: live conformance check, exit 0/1), 'model_check' (sim_plugins.model_check:main: checks a detector weights file before a flight, exit 0/1) and 'run_meta' (sim_plugins.run_meta:main: writes <run>/run_meta/{autopilot,detector,team_stack}.json).

Marks the folder as the Python package sim_plugins and explains the idea in its purpose text: the slots (autopilot, camera, detector, mission_brain, world, extras, network), what a profile is, and what each module does. Its __all__ lists the 13 modules.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: Importing it loads nothing heavy; scripts and launch files import only the modules they need.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: The AUTOPILOT slot: decides which ArduCopter program flies the simulated drone, with which parameter files and in which run folder. Choices: the default (~/sitl/arducopter = ArduCopter 4.6.3), a version downloaded by fetch_sitl.sh (~/sitl/versions/<V>/arducopter), any binary by path, a built ArduPilot source tree, or 'external' (the autopilot runs on another computer or container and only MAVLink and the physics link cross over). Extra parameter files (e.g. the real drone's Mission Planner .param) are cleaned by params.py and loaded after astra_sitl.parm. Every non-default flavour gets its own run folder ~/.astra_sim/sitl_I<I>_<tag>, so saved parameters (eeprom.bin) of one version never leak into another.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: Used by sim_bringup's sim.launch.py when one of its autopilot launch arguments (autopilot, sitl_version, sitl_bin, sitl_source, sitl_param_files, sitl_param_filter, sitl_param_keep, sitl_run_dir, sitl_wipe, mavlink_master, fdm_addr) is not at its default: it calls settings_from_launch, plan_autopilot, flavour_tag, patch_plugin_fdm_addr, mavproxy_master_args, remote_command and describe. plan.py uses settings_from_profile + to_launch_args to turn a profile's autopilot section into those arguments. Related network facts: SITL MAVLink TCP 5760+10I, physics UDP 9002+10I.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: The autopilot slot as plain values: mode ('sitl' or 'external'), version, binary, source_dir, extra param_files, param_filter ('safe'/'none'), param_keep, run_dir ('' = automatic), wipe (start SITL with -w), instance I, mavlink_master ('' = local SITL), fdm_addr ('' = the model's 127.0.0.1; external 0.0.0.0) and sim_address (only for the printed remote command).

True when the binary, parameter files or run folder differ from sim.launch.py's old code path (external mode, a version, a source tree, param files, an explicit run folder, a non-safe filter or kept names). sitl_bin, sitl_wipe and sitl_instance on their own are still handled by the old unchanged code.
True when nothing at all differs from today's simulator (no plan needed, no binary, no MAVLink master, no fdm_addr, no wipe).

Builds AutopilotSettings from a resolved profile's autopilot section: instance, wipe, filter, keep and param files; for kind 'external' the MAVLink address, fdm_addr (default 0.0.0.0) and sim_address (and param files/wipe are cleared, they do nothing there); for 'sitl_source' the source folder; otherwise version and binary.
Splits a comma-separated text into a list of trimmed, non-empty items.

Builds AutopilotSettings from sim.launch.py's argument texts (missing names get their defaults): 'external' or 'remote' means external mode, sitl_instance becomes the instance, comma lists become param files (with ~ expanded) and upper-cased keep names, sitl_wipe is read as a switch.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: by sim.launch.py when an autopilot launch argument is not at its default

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Inner helper: returns one launch argument's text, trimmed, or its default from LAUNCH_DEFAULTS when missing.

Turns AutopilotSettings back into the sim.launch.py arguments that select this autopilot, listing ONLY those that differ from the defaults (autopilot:=external, sitl_version, sitl_bin, sitl_source, sitl_param_files, sitl_param_filter, sitl_param_keep, sitl_wipe, mavlink_master, fdm_addr). A non-default flavour also gets sitl_run_dir so the plan shows exactly which folder SITL uses.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.outputs: an ordered dict of launch argument name -> text

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Returns the first 6 hex digits of the SHA-1 of a text (used to make short, unique folder tags).

Makes a short folder tag for a non-default autopilot, '' for the default: 'external', 'src-<tree name>-<hash>', 'bin-<hash>' (only when include_binary), 'v4.7.1', plus 'params-<hash>' when extra parameter files are used.
Returns today's SITL run folder for an instance: <sim_home>/sitl_I<I> (e.g. ~/.astra_sim/sitl_I0), the same as sim_paths.sitl_run_dir.
Returns the SITL run folder for these settings: the explicit run_dir if given, otherwise today's folder for the default, otherwise <sim_home>/sitl_I<I>_<tag>.
The run folder sim.launch.py uses for its arguments: like run_dir_for but an old sitl_bin:= on its own keeps today's folder (unchanged behaviour).
Returns where fetch_sitl.sh puts a version: <sitl_versions_dir>/<version>/ (e.g. ~/sitl/versions/4.7.1/).
Returns the SITL program inside a built ArduPilot source tree: <tree>/build/sitl/bin/arducopter.
Returns ArduPilot's stock parameter folder inside a source tree: <tree>/Tools/autotest/default_params.

Finds the default SITL program the same way as before profiles: uses sim_bringup's sim_paths.find_sitl_binary if it can be imported, otherwise checks $ARDUPILOT_SITL_BIN, ~/sitl/arducopter and Docker's /opt/ardupilot/build/sitl/bin/arducopter for an executable file. Returns None when none exists.

Finds a stock ArduPilot parameter file (copter.parm, gazebo-iris.parm): through sim_paths.find_param_file if possible, otherwise in $ARDUPILOT_DEFAULT_PARAMS, ~/sitl or /opt/ardupilot/Tools/autotest/default_params.

Reads an arducopter program in 1 MB pieces (up to 64 MB) looking for the text 'ArduCopter V<x.y.z> (<git hash>)' compiled into it, and returns e.g. '4.6.3 (3fc7011a)', or '' if not found or unreadable.
True when a file starts with the 4 bytes 7F 'ELF', i.e. it looks like a Linux program.

What will run for the autopilot slot: mode, the arducopter program and where it comes from (in plain words), its compiled version, the folder searched first for copter.parm / gazebo-iris.parm, a report per extra parameter file, the run folder, wipe, the MAVLink master, the plugin's fdm_addr, errors (each with a fix) and notes for the log.

Returns the paths of copter.parm and gazebo-iris.parm: from params_dir (the version or source tree) when they are there, otherwise from the default search, adding a note for each file taken elsewhere or not found.

Builds SITL's --defaults list in load order (later wins): the stock files, then sim_models' astra_sitl.parm (with a note that payload servos 11/13 are not set up if it is missing), then the cleaned extra parameter files.

Decides everything for these settings and returns an AutopilotPlan; for 'external' there is no program, mavlink_master is required and fdm_addr becomes 0.0.0.0 when empty. Otherwise it checks that the chosen program exists and is executable (given binary, <tree>/build/sitl/bin/arducopter, ~/sitl/versions/<V>/arducopter, or the default search), with an error naming the likely cause and the fix (chmod +x, git clone the tree, build it with ./waf, fetch_sitl.sh V, 02_setup_ardupilot.sh). It reads the compiled version and adds a note when the program has no ELF header or when its version does not start with the version asked for. Every extra parameter file is cleaned by params.prepare_param_file (written to ~/.astra_sim/generated/params unless it is a dry run); a missing file, or one with unreadable lines (params.report_errors), is an error.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: by sim.launch.py when the autopilot slot is not default (any plan error stops the launch with 'the autopilot cannot start'), and by plan.check_environment for profile_tool plan --check / shell

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: One line for the plan or the launch log: for external 'external autopilot: MAVProxy <- <address>; drone plugin listens on <fdm_addr>:<9002+10I>; run folder ...', otherwise 'SITL <program> = ArduCopter <version> + N parameter file(s) (<filter> filter); run folder ...'.

Returns, as text, the command that starts ArduCopter SITL on the OTHER computer for an external autopilot: 'arducopter --model JSON --sim-address=<this computer> -I<I> --home <home> --defaults copter.parm,gazebo-iris.parm,astra_sitl.parm'. sim.launch.py prints it in its log. SITL then sends physics packets to this computer's UDP 9002+10I and listens for MAVLink on TCP 5760+10I.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: by sim.launch.py with autopilot:=external

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Returns MAVProxy's '--master <address>' arguments, plus '--retries 300' for a remote TCP autopilot (about 5 minutes of tries instead of MAVProxy's default 3).

Edits a drone SDF text so the ArduPilotPlugin's <fdm_addr> has the given address (inserting the tag when missing). The plugin BINDS its JSON physics port (UDP 9002+10I) on this address: the model's 127.0.0.1 accepts only a SITL on the same computer, 0.0.0.0 accepts one on another computer/container. Returns (new text, whether an ArduPilotPlugin was found); an empty address changes nothing.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: by sim.launch.py for an external autopilot or an explicit fdm_addr

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Inner helper used for each ArduPilotPlugin block found: replaces an existing <fdm_addr>...</fdm_addr> or inserts one at the top of the block, and notes that a plugin was found.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: The CONFORMANCE CHECKER ('ros2 run sim_plugins check_slot --slot detector|mission_brain|team_stack|camera|autopilot|world|extras'). It looks at the LIVE ROS graph (and, for the camera, the network) and says in plain words whether the component filling a slot keeps that slot's contract: the topics it must publish/subscribe with the right message types and QoS, the services it must serve or call, and, when a sample message arrives, whether its fields make sense. Options --node, --timeout (60 s), --no-sample, --take-photo (presses the team's shutter /camera/trigger once), --photo-dir, --camera-ip, and for team_stack --skip-node / --add-node (repeatable, like stack_check). Exit code 0 = keeps the contract, 1 = something wrong, 2 = bad usage.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: Checks against contracts.py. The checks are plain functions over a Graph object: RosGraph reads the live graph through an rclpy node named 'check_slot', the unit tests use FakeGraph. Sample topics: /image_detection (detector, interfaces/ImageResult), /mavros/state (autopilot), /sim/drone/odometry (world); the camera slot uses siyi_probe.py to knock on 192.168.144.25 UDP 37260 and HTTP 82; the team_stack slot checks that all 7 Jetson nodes run and the MAVROS and team topics and services exist. Recommended in AGENTS.md's 'add a detector' recipe.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: One line of the result: level 'ok', 'fail' (breaks the contract), 'warn' (works, but check it) or 'info', the text, and an optional hint.
Formats the finding as ' OK ', ' XX ', ' !! ' or ' .. ' plus the text, and '-> hint' on a second line when there is one.
Everything check_slot found for one slot: the slot name, the component's node name and the list of findings.
Adds one finding (level, text, hint) to the report.
Property: True when any finding has level 'fail'.
Counts the findings per level: {'ok', 'fail', 'warn', 'info'}.
Prints the whole report: a 'check_slot: <slot> (component node: ...)' header, every finding, and 'RESULT: PASS (n check(s) passed, m warning(s))' or 'RESULT: FAIL (n problem(s), m warning(s))'.
A publisher or subscriber seen in the graph: which node, which message type, and its reliability ('reliable' or 'best_effort').

The list of questions the checks ask about the ROS graph: node names, publishers and subscribers of a topic, every service with its types, and per node the services it serves, the services it calls and the topics it publishes. RosGraph (live) and FakeGraph (tests) answer them.
Placeholder (raises NotImplementedError): the plain node names in the graph.
Placeholder (raises NotImplementedError): the publishers (Endpoints) of a topic.
Placeholder (raises NotImplementedError): the subscribers (Endpoints) of a topic.
Placeholder (raises NotImplementedError): every service in the graph with its type(s).
Placeholder (raises NotImplementedError): the services one node serves.
Placeholder (raises NotImplementedError): the services one node calls (its clients).
Placeholder (raises NotImplementedError): the topics one node publishes.
A pretend graph made of plain dicts (node list, publishers and subscribers per topic, servers and clients per node), used by the unit tests and doc examples so every rule is tested without ROS.
Stores the given nodes, publishers, subscribers, servers and clients.
Returns the stored node names.
Returns the stored publishers of a topic.
Returns the stored subscribers of a topic.
Collects every served service from all nodes with its types.
Returns the services one node serves.
Returns the services one node calls.
Builds the topics one node publishes from the stored publisher lists.
The live ROS graph, read through an rclpy node (the 'check_slot' node).
Remembers the rclpy node used to ask ROS.
Maps each node name to its namespace (needed by the per-node ROS calls).
Returns the sorted node names, leaving out hidden ones that start with '_'.
Static helper: reads a QoS profile's reliability as 'best_effort', 'reliable' or 'unknown'.
Asks ROS for the publishers of a topic (node, type, reliability).
Asks ROS for the subscribers of a topic (node, type, reliability).
Asks ROS for every service name and its types.
Runs one of rclpy's per-node queries for a node in its namespace; returns {} if the node is unknown or just went away.
Asks ROS which services a node serves.
Asks ROS which services a node calls.
Asks ROS which topics a node publishes.

Finds the node(s) that fill a slot, ignoring tool nodes (check_slot, stack_check, phase_monitor, demo_panel, demo_markers, score_run): the --node name if running; otherwise the team's default node (new_od, main_controller, siyi_emulator) first, then any node in the slot's main role (publishes /image_detection, calls /addWaypoint, publishes /sim/camera/photo_info).

Checks every topic rule of a contract for the component (or any node for autopilot/world): a missing required topic is a fail (with who publishes it instead), a wrong message type is a fail, a BEST_EFFORT publisher on a 'reliable' topic is a fail (the team's RELIABLE subscriber would never receive it), otherwise ok. It also warns when another node publishes the same required topic (run ONE component per slot).

Checks every service rule: for 'server' the component must serve it, for 'client' it must call it (the client must be created when the node starts so it can be seen). Missing required -> fail, wrong type -> fail, otherwise ok; it notes when a called service has no server yet (MAVROS or waypoint_manager not running?).
Checks an extra: warns if it publishes a topic owned by another slot (/image_detection, /camera/trigger, /camera/command, MAVROS setpoint topics), and lists everything it publishes.

Sanity-checks one interfaces/ImageResult sample: image_name must be just the file name (and should exist in the team photo folder), method must be set and must not start with 'truth_detector' (unless it is the truth detector), num_detections must match the parallel lists, and each detection needs class_id '0' (person) or '1' (tent), a score 0..1, a box with a positive width and height and a box centre that is not negative. Latitude/longitude must be a real position (0, 0 is only a warning).
Checks one mavros_msgs/State sample: ok when MAVROS is connected to the autopilot (shows mode and armed), fail otherwise with a hint to check MAVProxy's MAVROS output and launcher.sh's FCU_URL.
Checks one nav_msgs/Odometry sample from /sim/drone/odometry: ok when the drone's x, y, z are real numbers (shows them), fail otherwise.

Runs all checks of one slot on a graph: extras need --node and only get check_extras; team_stack only gets check_team_stack (with skip_nodes / add_nodes) and returns; other slots find their component (camera may have no ROS node: the network checks decide), run check_topics and check_services, add the camera probe findings, and check the sample message if one was wanted (detector, autopilot, world). In detector:=truth mode a sample from truth_detector is accepted with a warning.

The camera slot's network checks: runs siyi_probe.probe_sdk (SIYI SDK 0x02 on UDP 37260) and probe_media (HTTP getdirectories on port 82) against the camera address and turns each result into an ok/fail Finding.
Returns the team photo folder from sim_bringup's sim_paths.team_photo_dir(), or '' if sim_bringup is not available (then the 'photo exists' check is skipped).

Defines check_slot's options: --slot (required; every contract except network: detector, mission_brain, team_stack, camera, autopilot, world, extras), --node, --timeout (60), --no-sample, --take-photo, --photo-dir, --camera-ip (192.168.144.25), and --skip-node / --add-node (repeatable, team_stack only).

check_slot's command line: needs rclpy (exit 2 otherwise), creates the ROS node 'check_slot', lets discovery fill the graph for 2 s and re-evaluates until the graph part passes or time runs out, then (if the slot has a sample topic) subscribes for one sample message, optionally publishes /camera/trigger once (--take-photo, waiting at least 30 s for the result), runs the final evaluate with the camera probe and the --skip-node / --add-node lists, prints the report and returns 1 on fail, 0 on pass.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: ros2 run sim_plugins check_slot --slot ...
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.effects: creates ROS node check_slot; with --take-photo publishes one std_msgs/Bool on /camera/trigger (the team's shutter)

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: The written CONTRACT of every slot, kept as data: exactly what a component must do to replace the team's current one - which ROS topics it publishes or subscribes (name, message type, QoS), which services it serves or calls, which files it reads or writes, which network ports it uses, and the behaviour rules in plain words. Slots: autopilot, camera, detector, mission_brain, world, extras, network and team_stack (the whole Jetson code as one piece: its 7 node names, the MAVROS topics and services, /camera/trigger, /image_detection, /addWaypoint, a launcher.sh that honours TRACKER_CMD and FCU_URL, and the status texts the simulator parses). Taken from the team's code (new_od, main_controller, video_cam, waypoint_manager). Examples: a detector must publish ONE interfaces/msg/ImageResult per photo on /image_detection (RELIABLE), even when nothing is found; the camera must listen on UDP <camera_ip>:37260 and TCP :82, send 0x0B within 0.8 s and list the photo within 15 s; the team's MAVROS connects to SITL SERIAL2 at TCP 5763+10*I.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: The same data is used three ways: check_slot.py checks a running component against the machine-checkable rows, 'profile_tool contract --slot X' prints it, and doc_blocks.py writes it as tables into docs/simulation/PLUGINS.md (test_contracts.py keeps them in step). 'reliable' QoS matters because a BEST_EFFORT publisher never reaches main_controller's RELIABLE subscriber.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: One ROS topic in a contract: name, message type, role (what the COMPONENT does: 'publish' or 'subscribe'), QoS ('reliable', 'best_effort' or 'any'), whether it is required, and a note. Example: /image_detection, interfaces/msg/ImageResult, publish, reliable, required.
One ROS service in a contract: name, type, role ('server' or 'client'), required or not, and a note. Example: /addWaypoint, interfaces/srv/AddWaypoint, client, required (for the mission brain).
One file or folder in a contract that the component 'reads' or 'writes', with a note. Example: the team photo folder <ws>/src/video_cam/mapping_photos/"<lat> , <lon>.jpg" read by the detector.
One network port or link in a contract that the component 'listens' on or 'talks to', with a note. Example: 'UDP <camera_ip>:37260' listened on by the camera.

Everything a replacement for one slot must do: slot name, title, the default component, the alternatives, a summary, the node names the stack waits for, and the lists of topic, service, file and port rules plus plain-words behaviour rules.
Returns the contract of one slot by name; a typo raises KeyError listing the known slots (autopilot, camera, detector, mission_brain, world, extras, network, team_stack).

Turns a contract into plain text (profile_tool contract prints it): title, default, alternatives, summary, node names, then sections for ROS topics (role, name, type, QoS, REQUIRED/optional, note), services, files, network ports and numbered-style rules.
Escapes the '|' character so a note does not break a Markdown table.

Turns a contract into Markdown text: default, alternatives, summary, node names, then tables for topics, services, files and network, and a numbered rules list. doc_blocks.py uses it for the generated contract tables in docs/simulation/PLUGINS.md, and profile_tool contract --markdown prints it.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: Writes the GENERATED parts of docs/simulation/PLUGINS.md from the code so the page can never drift from what the tools really do: 'reference' (every profile key with its default, accepted values and help, from schema.py, plus the entry keys) and 'contracts' (every slot's contract as tables, from contracts.py). Each part sits between marker lines '<!-- BEGIN GENERATED <name>: ... -->' and '<!-- END GENERATED <name> -->'; only the text between them is rewritten.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: 'profile_tool docs --write' rewrites the parts, 'docs --check' exits 1 when one is out of date, and test_doc_blocks.py runs the check, so changing schema.py or contracts.py without regenerating the docs fails the tests.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Returns the line that opens a generated part: '<!-- BEGIN GENERATED <name>: python3 -m sim_plugins.profile_tool docs --write -->'.
Returns the line that closes a generated part: '<!-- END GENERATED <name> -->'.
Makes text safe inside a Markdown table cell: escapes '|' and turns line breaks into spaces.
Returns a default value the way it looks in a profile, as Markdown code: `null`, `true`/`false`, `[a, b]`, `""` for empty text, or the value itself.

Describes in words what values a key takes: 'one of `a`, `b`' (with aliases) for choices, 'a whole number min..max' for ints, otherwise the plain-words text for its kind (e.g. 'a port number 1..65535').

Builds the profile reference: an intro, then one Markdown table per section (Key | Default | Accepts | What it does), starting with the file's own keys, then an 'Entry keys' table explaining launch / executable / command and the other entry keys.

Builds the contract part: for each slot in the order detector, mission_brain, camera, autopilot, world, extras, network (and any new slot after them) an anchor like <a id="detector">, a heading and the contract tables from contracts.render_markdown.
Returns the body of one generated part ('reference' or 'contracts') without its marker lines.
Builds the regular expression that finds one generated part between its begin and end markers.
Puts freshly generated parts between their markers in a Markdown text and returns (new text, names of parts that changed, names whose markers are missing). Text outside the markers is never touched.
Returns the names of generated parts that are missing or differ from what the code says now (used by 'docs --check' and the test).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: Helpers that sim_bringup's launch files use to apply a plug-in profile: load_profile reads and checks a profile given as profile:=NAME_OR_PATH, apply_profile_args copies the profile's values into launch arguments the user left at their default (what the user typed always wins), and entry_actions turns one profile entry (custom detector, mission brain, camera or an extra) into launch actions: an included launch file, one node, or a plain program. Only entry_actions needs the ROS 2 launch libraries.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: sim.launch.py calls load_profile, apply_profile_args(..., plan.sim_args_full(...)) and entry_actions for plan.sim_side_entries (custom camera, simulator extras); team_stack.launch.py calls load_profile, apply_profile_args(..., team_args(...)) and entry_actions for plan.team_side_entries (custom detector/brain, team-stack extras). Living here means the same code serves both files and can be unit-tested.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Reads and checks a profile for a launch file (a name in simulation/profiles or a path) by calling profiles.resolve. Raises ProfileError listing every problem in plain words; the launch file prints them and stops.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: sim.launch.py / team_stack.launch.py with profile:=...

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Copies profile values into launch arguments that are still at their default value (changing the cfg dict in place) and returns [(name, old, new)] of every change for the launch log. An argument the user typed with a different value is never changed; typing exactly the default cannot be told apart from not typing it, so then the profile wins.
Returns the team_stack.launch.py arguments a profile decides: detector ('real', 'truth' or 'custom'), mission_brain, and for the team detector model_path (if set) and batched ('true'/'false').
Turns a YAML value into a launch-argument text: booleans become 'true'/'false', lists become comma-separated text, anything else its plain text.
Picks the right ROS 2 launch-description source by file extension: Python (.launch.py/.py), XML (.xml) or YAML (.yaml/.yml); anything else raises ValueError.

Builds the launch actions that start one profile entry: a 'launch' entry becomes IncludeLaunchDescription of <package share>/launch/<file> (or a path) with its args as launch arguments; an 'executable' entry becomes a Node (package, executable, name = node_name, parameters = args); a 'command' entry becomes ExecuteProcess with the word list (no shell). Each comes with a '[tag] starting ...' log line. A missing package or launch file becomes an '[tag] ERROR ... not started' log line and the entry is skipped, so the rest of the simulator still starts.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.effects: starts the teammate's component (launch file, ROS node or program) when the launch runs

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: Lets you use a REAL drone's ArduPilot parameter file in the simulator safely. Mission Planner can save all Pixhawk parameters to a .param file; loading it into SITL makes the simulated autopilot fly the mission like the real one (waypoint speed and radius, RTL height, failsafes). But lines about the PHYSICAL drone would break the simulator, so the 'safe' filter drops sensor calibrations (INS_, COMPASS_, BARO...), wiring (SERIAL, GPS, BATT, RC, CAN, BRD_...), the airframe and tuning (FRAME_, SERVO1-8_, MOT_, ATC_, PSC_) and the few values the simulator needs (SIM_, SERVO11/13_FUNCTION, FENCE_ENABLE, FS_GCS_ENABLE, AUTO_OPTIONS, PLND_ENABLED, MNT, SYSID). It reads Mission Planner .param, QGroundControl .params and ArduPilot .parm formats and writes a SITL --defaults file with one short 'NAME VALUE' per line.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: Called by autopilot.plan_autopilot for the profile keys autopilot.param_files, param_filter ('safe' or 'none') and param_keep (demo.sh --param-file). The cleaned copies go to <sim_home>/generated/params and are passed to SITL after ArduPilot's copter.parm, gazebo-iris.parm and sim_models' astra_sitl.parm. Unreadable lines are not silently skipped: report_errors turns them into plan errors (with line numbers and the fix), so sim.launch.py refuses to start with a damaged or wrong file.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: One parameter read from a file: its name, its value exactly as written, and the line number.
What happened to one input file: the source, the SITL defaults file written (or ''), the parameters kept, the (name, reason) of those dropped, the unreadable lines and plain-words warnings.
One line for the launch log or the plan: 'file.param: N parameter(s) used, M dropped by the filter, K unreadable line(s) -> output path'.
True when a text is a finite number (so 'nan', 'inf' and words are rejected).

Reads a parameter file's text line by line ('#' starts a comment): QGroundControl lines '1<TAB>1<TAB>NAME<TAB>VALUE<TAB>TYPE', or 'NAME,VALUE' / 'NAME VALUE' / 'NAME=VALUE'. Names are upper-cased and must be 1-16 characters of capitals, digits and _; values must be numbers of at most 32 characters (MAX_VALUE_CHARS). Later lines win for a repeated name.
Says why the filter drops a parameter (the reason text of the first matching DROP_RULES pattern), or '' when it is kept. Nothing is dropped in mode 'none' or for names listed in keep.
Splits a list of parameters into the kept ones and the dropped (name, reason) pairs using drop_reason.

Warns about settings of the REAL drone that would break its mission: if the file sets SERVO11_FUNCTION or SERVO13_FUNCTION to anything but 0, DO_SET_SERVO for the person (output 11) or tent (output 13) drop would be refused on the real drone. The text also says whether the simulator keeps 0 or uses the bad value.

Makes the text of a SITL --defaults file: a 3-line '#' header naming the source file and saying it is rewritten at every start, then one 'NAME VALUE' per kept parameter. Every line must stay within 89 characters (MAX_LINE_CHARS) because ArduPilot reads defaults files in 100-byte pieces; a longer line raises ValueError, a guard that parse_param_text's name and value limits should make impossible.
File name of the cleaned copy: <stem>_<first 8 hex digits of the SHA-1 of the full source path>.sim.parm, with unsafe characters replaced, so two files never clash and there are no spaces.

Reads, filters and (when write is true and a folder is given) saves one parameter file for SITL. It never raises for a bad file: an unreadable file, bad lines, real-drone warnings and 'no NAME VALUE lines' all go into the returned ParamFileReport.
Runs prepare_param_file for each file in order (later files win in SITL, like --defaults a,b,c) and returns the reports.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: The few folders sim_plugins needs, found with the same rules as sim_bringup/sim_paths.py but without importing it: sim_home ($ASTRA_SIM_HOME or ~/.astra_sim), generated_dir (<sim_home>/generated), repo_dir ($ASTRA_REPO, else the checkout this file is in, else ~/ODLC_Machine_Inferencing_System_2025-2026), profiles_dir ($ASTRA_PROFILES_DIR or <repo>/simulation/profiles), sitl_dir ($ASTRA_SITL_DIR or ~/sitl) and sitl_versions_dir ($ASTRA_SITL_VERSIONS or <sitl_dir>/versions).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: A copy instead of an import because sim_bringup's launch files import sim_plugins, so sim_plugins must work without sim_bringup (no circular dependency; tests run on any computer). Used by profiles.py, autopilot.py, plan.py and profile_tool.py.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Expands '~' and $VARIABLES in a path text; an empty text stays empty.
Reads an on/off switch: True for the boolean True or the texts '1', 'true', 'yes', 'on' (any case), False for anything else. Launch arguments always arrive as text, so this is how switches are read.
Returns the folder for everything the simulator writes at run time: $ASTRA_SIM_HOME, or ~/.astra_sim.
Returns <sim_home>/generated, where run-time files go: resolved profiles, cleaned parameter files, filtered launch files.

Returns the team repo the simulator runs from: $ASTRA_REPO (set by simulation/setup/sim_env.sh); otherwise the first parent folder of this file that has both simulation/profiles and ros2_ws; otherwise ~/ODLC_Machine_Inferencing_System_2025-2026 (the Linux-side copy made by 03_build.sh).
Returns where the shared profiles live: $ASTRA_PROFILES_DIR, else <repo>/simulation/profiles.
Returns the native SITL folder made by simulation/setup/02_setup_ardupilot.sh: $ASTRA_SITL_DIR, else ~/sitl (the default ArduCopter 4.6.3 binary is ~/sitl/arducopter).
Returns where simulation/setup/fetch_sitl.sh puts other SITL versions: $ASTRA_SITL_VERSIONS, else <sitl_dir>/versions (one sub-folder per version).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: Turns a resolved profile into what the scripts and launch files need: launch arguments for sim.launch.py and team_stack.launch.py, extra stack_check options, the shell variables demo.sh and start_sim.sh read, checks that every needed file, program and package exists on this computer, and the printable plan ('which component fills which slot'). The rule that keeps today's behaviour: only settings that DIFFER from the defaults produce extra arguments, so with no profile (or default.yaml) the commands are byte for byte the old ones.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: profile_tool.py calls demo_vars / start_sim_vars (for 'profile_tool shell', which demo.sh and start_sim.sh eval), summary_lines / render_summary and check_environment (for 'plan --check'). sim.launch.py calls sim_args_full and sim_side_entries; team_stack.launch.py calls team_side_entries. It also decides MAVROS's fcu_url for the team stack (default_fcu_url).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Converts the profile's camera.zoom into sim.launch.py's camera_max_zoom text: 'survey' -> '1' (photos keep the full 81 deg view), 'team' -> '' (camera default, so video_cam's 5x zoom rack works), a number -> that number.
Lists (role, entry) of everything team_stack.launch.py must start from the profile: a custom detector, a custom mission brain, and extras with start_with 'team_stack'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: by team_stack.launch.py with profile:=, and when planning

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Lists (role, entry) of everything sim.launch.py must start from the profile: a custom camera and extras with start_with 'simulator'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: by sim.launch.py with profile:=, and when planning

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: True when a launch file must read the profile itself because it has entries (custom components or extras) that cannot be passed as simple launch arguments.
Says where the resolved profile is written: <sim_home>/generated/profile_<name>_<6 hex of its content>.yaml (the content hash means a changed profile gets a new file).
Writes the resolved profile YAML to resolved_file_path and returns the path.

Builds every sim.launch.py argument this profile decides, defaults included: world, camera_model, detector (team -> 'real'), sitl_instance, gcs/mavros/panel ports, windows_gcs and its address, camera_max_zoom, gui/rviz/panel (off when headless), emulator (true only for kind siyi_emulator), camera_ip, camera_bind, camera_strict, MAVProxy outputs, and the autopilot arguments from autopilot.to_launch_args.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: by sim.launch.py with profile:= (through launch_support.apply_profile_args) and by demo_vars / start_sim_vars

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Keeps only the arguments whose value differs from the launch file's default (SIM_LAUNCH_DEFAULTS, which test_plan.py compares with sim.launch.py itself).

Builds extra stack_check options for replaced team nodes: '--skip-node new_od' for a custom detector and '--skip-node main_controller' for a custom mission brain, each followed by '--add-node <node_name>' when the entry names its node.

True when demo.sh should wait for the detector's model to load (stack_check --need-detector): always for the team detector, for a custom one only if it says provides_health, never for the truth detector.
Builds team_stack.launch.py arguments beyond detector:=...: model_path:= and batched:=true for the team detector, mission_brain:=custom, and profile:=<resolved file> when there are team-side entries.

Picks MAVROS's fcu_url when the profile does not set network.fcu_url: with a local SITL, tcp://127.0.0.1:<5763 + 10 x instance>, i.e. SITL's SERIAL2 directly, wired like the real Jetson on the Pixhawk's TELEM2, so the team's status texts reach the ground-station side like on the real drone; with an external autopilot, MAVProxy's MAVROS output udp://:<mavros_port>@localhost:<mavros_port>.
Variables for a bash script: scalars (NAME=value) and arrays (NAME=(a b c)).

Returns the variables as text lines a bash script can 'eval' (NAME=value, and NAME=(a b c) for lists), every value quoted safely with shlex.quote. profile_tool shell prints that text and demo.sh / start_sim.sh eval it.

Everything demo.sh needs from a profile: WORLD, DETECTOR, CAMERA, ZOOM, HEADLESS, TIMEOUT_MIN, INSTANCE, the three ports, WINDOWS_GCS(_ADDR), MISSION_OVERRIDE, MODEL_OVERRIDE, FCU_URL_OVERRIDE, TEAM_STACK_WHERE, TEAM_REPO ('' = demo.sh's own copy of the team code), NEED_DETECTOR, CAMERA_KIND, CAMERA_IP, PLUGIN_PROFILE(_FILE), PLUGIN_DETECTOR_TEXT, PLUGIN_SUMMARY, and the arrays PLUGIN_SIM_ARGS (non-default sim.launch.py arguments demo.sh does not set itself, + profile:=), PLUGIN_TEAM_ARGS and PLUGIN_STACK_ARGS.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: demo.sh --profile ... (through 'profile_tool shell --for demo')

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Everything start_sim.sh needs: WORLD, PLUGIN_PROFILE(_FILE), PLUGIN_SUMMARY, PLUGIN_TEAM_HINT and PLUGIN_SIM_ARGS (non-default launch arguments the user did not type). camera_max_zoom is only added when it is not '1', because start_sim.sh already adds camera_max_zoom:=1 itself.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: start_sim.sh --profile ... (through 'profile_tool shell --for start_sim')

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Builds the command for terminal 2 (the team stack) that matches the profile, e.g. FCU_URL=tcp://127.0.0.1:5763 TRACKER_CMD="ros2 launch sim_bringup team_stack.launch.py" ./launcher.sh sim, adding only non-default team arguments. FCU_URL is always written because launcher.sh sim's own default is still MAVProxy's udp 14552 output. With run.team_repo the command starts with 'cd <that checkout> && ', because another checkout of the team code runs its own launcher.sh.
Describes a custom entry in a few words: '<package> <launch file>', 'ros2 run <package> <executable>' or the command, plus '(arg=value, ...)'.

Describes the detector slot in words: 'team: detection/new_od (YOLO weights ...)', 'truth: sim_demo truth_detector (answer-key stand-in; new_od idles on an empty folder)', or 'custom: ... (replaces new_od)'.

Makes (slot, text) lines for every slot: world and mission, autopilot (from the environment check's plan when available, else from the profile, with its run folder), camera (siyi_emulator model, 2K/4K, zoom, strict/permissive, or custom/none), detector, mission brain, extras, network (MAVProxy master and every output, camera address) and team stack (local ./launcher.sh sim, '<checkout>/launcher.sh sim' when run.team_repo names another checkout, or external; plus MAVROS fcu_url).

Returns the slot table as text, the first part of every plan: a 'PROFILE <name> (<file>; overrides ...)' header, one line per slot (the environment check's autopilot notes shown under the autopilot line), then '!!' warning lines.
Returns a ROS package's installed share folder, None when the package is not installed, or '?' when ROS's ament_index is not available (so checks are skipped, not failed).
Returns a ROS package's install prefix, None when it is not installed, or '?' when ament_index is not available.

Finds an entry's launch file: an absolute path must exist; a bare name is looked for in <package share>/launch/ and <package share>/. Returns (absolute path, problem text), with problems such as 'ROS package X is not built/installed' or 'X is not in .../launch (is it installed by setup.py data_files?)'.
Lists what is missing on this computer for one custom entry: its launch file, its package or executable (lib/<package>/<executable>), or its command's program (a file or something on PATH).

Checks this computer for everything the profile needs, writing nothing: plans the autopilot with the same run folder the scripts will use (parameter files filtered only in memory), checks every custom entry, the world file and the mission file, runs model_check.quick_check on the team detector's weights (exists, format, a real PyTorch file, TensorRT present; no fingerprint), and, when run.team_repo names another checkout of the team code, runs team_repo.check on it (only a warning when run.team_stack is external). Its problems are prefixed 'detector model:' or 'team code:'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: profile_tool plan --check, profile_tool validate --check, and profile_tool shell (what demo.sh and start_sim.sh run in plug-in mode) unless --no-check is given (the scripts never give it)

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: The command line for plug-in profiles ('ros2 run sim_plugins profile_tool ...' or 'python3 -m sim_plugins.profile_tool ...'). Sub-commands: list (profiles in simulation/profiles), validate [--check] (check profiles, and with --check that every file/program exists here), plan --profile P [--set K=V] [--check] (which component fills each slot + the resulting arguments), resolve (complete settings as YAML), contract --slot S [--markdown], shell --for demo|start_sim (shell variables for the scripts), docs --check|--write (the generated parts of PLUGINS.md). Exit codes: 0 fine, 1 a problem in the profile or a missing file, 2 bad usage.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: Teammates use it to check a profile before a run. simulation/scripts/demo.sh and start_sim.sh run 'python3 -m sim_plugins.profile_tool shell --for demo|start_sim ...' and eval the printed PLUGIN_* variables into their launch commands. It is a thin layer over profiles.py, plan.py, contracts.py and doc_blocks.py.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Prints each problem as ' XX <text>' (to stderr unless another stream is given); accepts plain texts or Problem objects.
Resolves the profile named by the command's --profile and --set options (and --profiles-dir) through profiles.resolve.
'list': prints every profile in the profiles folder with its description, or 'BROKEN: <first error>' for one that does not load. Exit 1 if none were found or any is broken.

'validate': checks the named profiles (all in the folder if none are named), printing ' OK name' with its warnings or ' XX name: <problems>'. With --check it also runs plan.check_environment and reports what is missing on this computer. Exit 1 if any failed.
'resolve': prints the complete settings (defaults + extends + file + overrides) as self-contained YAML, or the problems and exit 1.

Builds the printable plan: the slot table (plan.render_summary), then COMMANDS: the sim.launch.py arguments that differ from the defaults (+ profile:= if needed), the team_stack.launch.py arguments, extra stack_check options (+ --need-detector), and, unless it is for demo.sh, the team-stack command for terminal 2.
'plan': resolves the profile, optionally checks this computer (--check), and prints the plan; with --check and something missing it prints 'MISSING ON THIS COMPUTER:' and exits 1.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: python3 -m sim_plugins.profile_tool plan --profile NAME --check (AGENTS.md recipe step 4)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: 'shell': resolves the profile, checks this computer unless --no-check (missing things -> stderr, exit 1), prints warnings to stderr, writes the resolved profile file when needed (not with --no-write), and prints the shell variables from plan.demo_vars or plan.start_sim_vars (with the names the user typed, --typed) for the script to eval.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: by demo.sh in plug-in mode (--profile, --set, --detector custom, or a plug-in option such as --sitl-version, --param-file, --autopilot, --fcu-url) and by start_sim.sh with --profile or --set

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: 'contract': prints the contract of one slot (or all) as plain text, or with --markdown as the Markdown tables; an unknown slot exits 2.

'docs': with no flag prints both generated parts with their markers; with --check compares them with docs/simulation/PLUGINS.md (or --file) and exits 1 when one is out of date or its markers are missing; with --write rewrites only the parts between the markers.
Builds the argument parser: the global --profiles-dir and the sub-commands list, validate, resolve, plan, shell, contract and docs with their options.
Inner helper: adds the shared --profile (name or path, '' = built-in defaults) and repeatable --set KEY=VALUE options to a sub-command.
Command-line entry point: parses the arguments, runs the chosen sub-command and returns its exit code; a ProfileError anywhere is printed as ' XX ...' and returns 1.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: ros2 run sim_plugins profile_tool ... / python3 -m sim_plugins.profile_tool ...

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: Reads a plug-in profile (a small YAML file), checks every value against schema.py, and produces the complete settings the simulator will use. Order (later wins): built-in defaults, then the profile it 'extends:' (recursively), then the file itself, then command-line overrides like '--set detector.kind=truth'. Every mistake is reported at once in plain words, with a hint and 'did you mean ...?' for typos. Relative paths inside a profile are relative to that profile's folder.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: The heart of the profile system: profile_tool.py (validate, plan, resolve, list, shell), launch_support.py (sim_bringup's launch files) and plan.py all start from resolve(). Profiles are found by name in simulation/profiles/ or by path; the result can be written to <sim_home>/generated/profile_<name>.yaml for the launch files.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: One thing wrong (or worth a warning) in a profile: where (the key, e.g. 'detector.kind' or 'extras[1].launch'), the message in plain words, a hint how to fix it, the severity ('error' stops the start, 'warning' is only printed) and the file it came from.
Formats the problem as one or two printable lines: 'key (file): message' and, if there is a hint, '-> hint' below it.
The exception raised when a profile cannot be used; its .problems list holds every error (and the warnings found so far).
Stores the problems and sets the short message 'N problem(s) in the profile' (N counts only errors).
Builds the full printable report: 'N problem(s) in the profile:' with one line per error, then 'and warning(s):' with the warnings.
Finds the closest valid option to a misspelt word (difflib, similarity 0.6 or more) and returns 'did you mean "X"?', or '' when nothing is close.

The complete, checked settings after defaults + extends + file + overrides: the nested settings dict (same shape as schema.defaults()), the profile name ('(built-in defaults)' without a file), the files read (base first), the warnings and the --set overrides applied.
Returns the value at a dotted key like 'detector.kind' (or the given default when it is missing).
Property: the profile file that was asked for (the last file read), or '' for the built-in defaults.
True when the settings are exactly the built-in defaults (ignoring the descriptive keys), i.e. the simulator will behave exactly as today.
Returns a copy of the settings without the descriptive keys profile, name, description and extends, so only what changes behaviour is compared.

Turns a profile reference into a file path: an absolute or ~ path, a path relative to the given folder or the current folder, or a NAME in the profiles folder ('truth_detector' or 'truth_detector.yaml'; '.yaml' is added when missing). If nothing matches it raises ProfileError with 'did you mean' and the list of known profiles.

Reads one profile file with PyYAML. It must be a mapping ('key: value' lines); an empty file counts as {}. A YAML mistake becomes a ProfileError saying the line and column, with the hint to check indentation (spaces, not tabs) and colons.
Reads a yes/no value from YAML booleans, 0/1 or the words true/yes/on/1 and false/no/off/0; returns None when it is not a yes/no value.
Expands ~ and $VARIABLES and makes a relative path relative to the profile's folder; Linux paths starting with / are normalised with forward slashes so tests also pass on Windows.
True for texts that look like a file location (contain a slash, or start with ~, $ or .), False for a bare name like 'my_file.launch.py'.
Checks a 'HOST:PORT' text: needs both parts, no spaces in the host, and a whole-number port 1..65535. Returns None when fine, otherwise the reason.

Checks a MAVProxy address like 'udp:127.0.0.1:14552': it must start with one of the allowed kinds (udp, udpout, udpbcast, tcp, tcpin for outputs; also udpin for a master) followed by HOST:PORT, or be a /dev/... serial port. Returns None when fine, else the reason.

Checks and cleans one value against its schema Field and returns the clean value. Each kind has its rule: bool (yes/no words), int/port (whole numbers in range, ports 1..65535), choice (lower-cased, aliases applied), zoom ('survey', 'team' or 0 < x <= 30), path(s) (resolved), names (ArduPilot parameter names), mavout/mavurl (MAVProxy addresses), ip (IPv4), hostport, version (strips 'Copter-' or 'v'), entry/entries (check_entry). A bad value adds a Problem and falls back to the default.
Inner helper of check_value: records a Problem for this key (the hint defaults to the key's help line) and returns a copy of the key's default value.

Makes a short default name for a 'command' entry from the program or script it runs, skipping options (words starting with -) and launcher programs (python3, bash, env ...): ['python3', '/home/me/logger.py', '--fast'] -> 'logger'.

Checks one custom-component entry (detector.custom, mission_brain.custom, camera.custom or an extras item): only known keys (name, package, launch, executable, command, args, node_name, provides_health, start_with), exactly ONE of launch / executable / command, an executable or a bare launch name needs its package, start_with only for extras (team_stack or simulator). Fills a default name. Returns the clean entry or None.

Checks a partial profile mapping against a schema (sub)table and returns only the keys that were given, cleaned. Unknown keys become problems with 'did you mean'; 'world: runway' is accepted as short for world.name; a world name ending in .sdf/.yaml or looking like a path is resolved as a path.
Deep-merges two settings dicts: mappings merge key by key, anything else (lists too) is replaced by the overlay. Custom entries and their args are replaced whole, not merged.

Splits a command-line override 'section.key=value' into (dotted key, value). The value stays text (check_value converts it later) because YAML would turn some addresses and times into numbers; only values starting with [ or { are read as YAML, and null / ~ mean 'nothing'. A text without '=' raises ProfileError.
Reads a value as YAML (so '0.5' becomes a number and 'true' a boolean); returns the text itself when it is not valid YAML.
Turns a dotted key and a value into nested dicts: 'a.b.c', 1 -> {'a': {'b': {'c': 1}}}.

Turns a list of --set overrides into one checked partial profile (paths relative to the current folder). Overrides inside a custom entry, like 'detector.custom.args.threshold=0.5', are returned separately (read as YAML) so resolve() can apply them to the entry the profile already has.

Checks that need several keys together on the merged settings: kind custom needs a custom entry (and an entry with another kind is ignored, warning); sitl_source needs source_dir; external needs a MAVLink address; version OR binary, not both; gcs/mavros/panel ports must differ; moving gcs_out warns that demo.sh and the mission scripts will not reach the autopilot; a custom detector/brain without node_name warns that demo.sh cannot wait for it; a model path with a space is an error, and a model path with a detector kind other than team warns that it is ignored; a run.team_repo path with a space is an error; an external team stack warns about team-side pieces it will not start; duplicate extras names warn.

Builds the complete, checked settings: starts from schema.defaults(); if a profile is named, follows its 'extends:' chain (stopping with an error on a circle), checks and merges each file base first; applies the --set overrides (including ones inside custom entries); runs cross_checks. Raises ProfileError listing EVERY error; warnings go into the result.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: by every profile_tool command, by plan.py and by launch_support.load_profile (sim.launch.py / team_stack.launch.py with profile:=)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Returns the resolved settings as one self-contained YAML text (extends cleared, paths absolute) with a header saying which files and overrides it was made from and 'Do not edit: it is rewritten at every start'. write_resolved and plan.write_resolved_file save that text to a file; profile_tool resolve prints it.
Saves dump_resolved() as <sim_home>/generated/profile_<name>.yaml (unsafe characters in the name become _) and returns the path.
Goes through every *.yaml in the profiles folder, tries to resolve each one, and returns (name, description, problem) for each; problem is '' when it loads fine or the first line of the error.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: The one table of every key a profile may contain, with its default value, how it is checked and one line of help. Sections: world (name 'runway', mission), autopilot (kind sitl_binary/sitl_source/external, version, binary, source_dir, param_files, param_filter 'safe', param_keep, wipe, instance 0, external.mavlink/fdm_addr/sim_address), camera (kind siyi_emulator/custom/none, model zr10/a8mini, zoom 'survey', strict, custom), detector (kind team/truth/custom, model_path, batched, custom), mission_brain (team/custom), extras (a list), network (gcs_port 14550, mavros_port 14552, panel_port 14553, outputs, windows_gcs, camera_ip 192.168.144.25, camera_bind, fcu_url) and run (headless, timeout_min 30, team_stack local/external, team_repo '' = the simulator's own copy of the team code). The defaults are exactly today's simulator behaviour.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: Drives everything else: profiles.py validates against it, plan.py compares with its defaults (only differences become launch arguments), doc_blocks.py prints it as the profile reference in docs/simulation/PLUGINS.md, and test_profiles.py checks that simulation/profiles/default.yaml says the same thing.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: A read-only description of one profile key: its default (today's behaviour), its kind (how the value is checked: str, bool, int, port, choice, zoom, path, paths, names, mavout, mavouts, mavurl, ip, hostport, version, entry, entries), the allowed choices, other spellings (aliases such as 'real' -> 'team'), the smallest and largest number allowed, and one help line used in errors and docs.
Builds the nested dict of default values for a table or sub-table, copying each default so callers can change their copy safely.

Returns a fresh copy of all built-in defaults: exactly how the simulator behaves with no profile (runway world, ArduCopter 4.6.3 from ~/sitl, siyi_emulator zr10 with survey zoom, the team detector and mission brain, ports 14550/14552/14553...).
Returns the Field (or section dict) at a dotted key such as 'detector.kind'; an unknown key raises KeyError.
Walks the table and yields every dotted key with its Field in table order, e.g. ('camera.model', Field(...)). Used by the docs and by 'did you mean' suggestions.
