mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: Knocks on a SIYI-compatible camera from outside, the way the team's video_cam does, to check the CAMERA slot (siyi_emulator or a teammate's own camera program): probe_sdk sends the SDK 'request hardware ID' frame (command 0x02) to UDP 37260 and waits for the answer; probe_media asks the media web API on TCP 82 for its photo folders (getdirectories?media_type=0) and checks the answer is JSON with a 'data' part. Standard library only, with its own tiny frame builder and CRC-16/XMODEM.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: Used by check_slot.camera_findings for 'check_slot --slot camera' (default address 192.168.144.25). It deliberately does not import siyi_emulator, so it also tests a camera program that is not ours.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Computes the CRC-16/XMODEM checksum the SIYI SDK uses (polynomial 0x1021, start value 0, no reflection) bit by bit in plain Python.

Builds one SIYI SDK frame: 55 66, CTRL (0x01 = 'please answer', else 0x00), data length and sequence number (2 bytes each, little-endian), the command number, the data and the CRC-16 of everything before it.
Finds the first 55 66 in a buffer and reads that frame: returns (command number, data) when it is complete and its checksum matches, otherwise None.

Sends the 0x02 hardware-ID request to UDP <ip>:37260 and waits (2 s by default) for a 0x02 answer. Returns (True, 'SIYI SDK answers on UDP ... (hardware id "6B...")') or (False, a reason such as 'no answer ... is the camera emulator running, and does this computer have that address? simulation/setup/camera_ip_alias.sh').
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.effects: one UDP packet to the camera

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: GETs http://<ip>:82/cgi-bin/media.cgi/api/v1/getdirectories?media_type=0 (3 s timeout) and checks the reply is JSON with a 'data' part. Returns (True, 'media web API answers ...') or (False, why: no answer, not JSON, or no 'data').

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: Makes a copy of the team's main/launch/tracker.launch.xml WITHOUT the nodes a profile replaces (detection/new_od for a custom detector, main/main_controller.py for a custom mission brain), so the teammate's component runs INSTEAD of the team's. Running both would break things: main_controller cannot tell two detectors apart, two mission brains fight over flight modes, and new_od loads YOLO onto the graphics card Gazebo shares. The team's file itself is never changed.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: Called by sim_bringup's team_stack.launch.py (write_filtered into the generated folder) only when a profile replaces a node; without a profile it includes the original tracker.launch.xml exactly as before.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Removes every <node pkg=P exec=E> listed in 'remove' from a ROS 2 XML launch file text (also inside <group>), keeps everything else, drops XML comments, and adds a 'GENERATED by sim_plugins ... Do not edit' header. Returns (new XML text, list of 'pkg/exec' removed). Text that is not valid XML, or whose root is not <launch>, raises ValueError.
Inner helper: goes through an XML element's children, removing matching <node> elements and descending into everything else (so nodes inside <group> are found).

Reads the team's tracker.launch.xml, filters it, and writes the copy as <out_dir>/tracker_without_<exec names>.launch.xml (e.g. tracker_without_new_od.launch.xml). Returns (path of the copy, removed list, notes); a node asked for but not in the file is only noted (the copy is still written).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: team_stack.launch.py with a profile whose detector or mission_brain is custom
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.effects: writes the filtered launch file into ~/.astra_sim/generated/

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/t.explain: Shared pytest helpers for the sim_plugins tests: puts the SOURCE folders of sim_plugins and sim_bringup on the Python path (tests run without building and test the files you just edited), paths inside the repo (REPO, PROFILES, SIM), a temporary ~/.astra_sim and ~/sitl per test, fake_arducopter (writes a tiny executable that looks like an ArduCopter SITL program: ELF header + version text), and include_location (works out which launch file an IncludeLaunchDescription really loads).

One command that runs every quick check of the plug-and-play part, without starting Gazebo, SITL or any ROS node: pytest for sim_plugins and the two sim_plugin_examples templates, validation of every profile in simulation/profiles, bash -n + shellcheck on demo.sh, start_sim.sh, fetch_sitl.sh and itself, fetch_sitl.sh --dry-run for a few versions, and the key proof that demo.sh --dry-run and start_sim.sh --dry-run print exactly the same commands with and without --profile default. Exit 0 = all passed, 1 = something failed (listed at the end).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/te.explain: Prints a coloured '==> <title>' heading before each test step.
Runs one check command: prints ' OK  <name>' when it succeeds, otherwise ' XX  <name>' and remembers the name in the FAILED list for the final summary.

Unit tests of the small plug-and-play hooks inside sim_bringup: stack_check --skip-node / --add-node, every plug-and-play argument of sim.launch.py has a 'today's behaviour' default and help text, and team_stack.launch.py declares detector / mission_brain / profile with today's defaults. The launch files are read as text, so no ROS is needed.

Unit tests of check_slot.py with fakes (FakeGraph for the ROS graph, SimpleNamespace objects for messages): the team's new_od passes, a BEST_EFFORT / wrong-type / missing publisher fails, a second detector warns, the mission brain's service clients are checked, sample messages are sanity-checked, and the camera probe results are reported.

Unit tests of siyi_probe.py: the SDK frame and CRC match the team's constant photo packet, frames round-trip, and both probes work against tiny fake servers on 127.0.0.1 (a UDP 'camera' that answers 0x02, an HTTP media API) and fail politely when nothing answers.

Unit tests of tracker_filter.py on the REAL main/launch/tracker.launch.xml: a custom detector removes exactly new_od, a custom mission brain exactly main_controller.py, everything else stays, and the team file is never changed.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: The package's guide in plain words: a diagram of video_cam <-> emulator <-> Gazebo, copy-paste quick start, how one photo flows and why the timings matter (0.8 s for 0x0B, 0.5 s deadline, 10 s frame wait), the strict A8-mini mode, the two camera models, every SDK command and HTTP request with its reply, the Gazebo and ROS topics, every parameter with its default, networking (192.168.144.25 alias, port 82), optical zoom, tests, troubleshooting and known team-code hazards it makes visible (5x zoom rack, photo names overwritten while hovering).

Every emulator parameter with its default value and unit in one place (the same values as the built-in defaults): camera_model zr10, strict false, camera_ip 192.168.144.25, ctrl_port 37260, media_port 82, sd_card_dir, photo_dir_name 101SIYI_IMG, jpeg_quality 92, photo_timeout_s 10, feedback_deadline_s 0.5, initial_pitch_deg -90, max_slew_dps 90, control_rate_hz 50, the gz topic names, joint names, hfov_rad 1.4137 and the two ROS extra topics.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: Loaded first by launch/siyi_emulator.launch.py and by sim_bringup's sim.launch.py, which then add their own overrides (camera_model, camera_ip, sd_card_dir, max_zoom ...).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: Launch file that starts the emulator node with config/siyi_emulator.yaml plus the most common settings as launch arguments (camera_model, strict, camera_ip, bind_ip, ctrl_port, media_port, use_gazebo, initial_pitch_deg, sd_card_dir, log_commands), e.g. 'ros2 launch siyi_emulator siyi_emulator.launch.py camera_model:=a8mini strict:=true'. Any other parameter can be changed with params_file:=<your copy of the YAML>.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: For starting the emulator by hand or from another launch file; the full simulator (sim.launch.py) creates the same node itself.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Builds the launch description: a params_file argument (default: the installed config/siyi_emulator.yaml), one launch argument per entry of ARGUMENTS whose value is converted to the right type (text, true/false, whole number, decimal), and the Node package siyi_emulator / executable siyi_emulator / name siyi_emulator with the YAML first and the overrides second (later wins).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: ros2 launch siyi_emulator siyi_emulator.launch.py

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: ROS 2 package manifest of siyi_emulator (version 1.0.0, ament_python, maintainer astra-sim@example.com, Apache-2.0). It lists what the emulator needs to run: rclpy, std_msgs, rcl_interfaces, numpy, OpenCV, PyYAML, launch and launch_ros (the Gazebo Python bindings are optional), and pytest for tests.
An empty marker file that registers the package name in the ament index, so ROS 2 tools (ros2 run, ros2 pkg prefix) can find siyi_emulator.

Gives this computer the SIYI camera's address so video_cam can reach the emulator: needs sudo, adds 192.168.144.25/32 (or the address given) to the loopback interface 'lo' if it is not there yet, and lowers net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start to 80 so normal users may open port 82. Safe to run twice; the address is lost at reboot or 'wsl --shutdown'.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.effects: changes network settings: ip addr add <ip>/32 dev lo; sysctl net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=80

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: Undoes add_camera_ip.sh: with sudo, removes the camera address (default 192.168.144.25) from the loopback interface if it is there. Only use it when no emulator or simulation (also in another WSL distro, which shares the network) still needs it.

Runs all of the package's pytest tests (python3 -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q test/, extra arguments passed on). It finds the package's test folder next to itself (source tree, installed share folder, or behind a symlink-install link). No Gazebo or ROS nodes needed; it only uses free ports on 127.0.0.1, so it never disturbs a running simulation.
Tells colcon/setuptools to put the two executables in lib/siyi_emulator, where 'ros2 run siyi_emulator ...' looks for them.

Build and install recipe of the Python package. It installs the modules, the launch file, config/siyi_emulator.yaml, the helper scripts, the tests and the Gazebo test fixture, and creates two commands: 'siyi_emulator' (siyi_emulator.node:main, the emulator) and 'siyi_client' (siyi_emulator.sdk_client:main, the tiny client).
Marks the folder as the Python package siyi_emulator, sets __version__ = '1.0.0' and lists in its purpose text what each module does.

Everything the pretend camera 'remembers' that is not the gimbal: which model it pretends to be (ZR10 or A8 mini), the zoom (which takes time to travel, like a real lens), the recording and HDR flags, whether the micro SD ('TF') card is in, and the exact bytes of the answers to commands 0x01 (firmware), 0x02 (hardware ID) and 0x0A (system info). Time is passed in as a number, so the zoom can be tested without waiting.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: command_handler.py asks it what to answer; emulator.py creates it from the parameters camera_model, strict, max_zoom, photo_width/photo_height and zoom_speed_x_per_s, and reads its zoom when it makes each photo. The two model profiles decide the photo size video_cam sees: ZR10 2560x1440 ('2K'), A8 mini 3840x2160 ('4K').

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: A read-only record of fixed facts about one SIYI camera model: short key ('zr10'/'a8mini'), display name, product ID byte (0x6B ZR10, 0x73 A8 mini), photo size, maximum zoom and how much of it is optical, yaw/pitch limits (-135..135 and -90..25 deg for both), which command answers 0x41, the length of the 0x0A answer (8 or 7 bytes), firmware version numbers and lens field of view (61.5 deg ZR10, 81 deg A8 mini).

Property: the 12-character hardware ID text the camera reports for command 0x02. The first two characters are the product ID in hex ('6B' or '73') followed by '0000000001'. video_cam reads only those first two characters to decide ZR10 or A8MINI.
Turns any spelling of a model name ('A8 mini', 'A8_MINI', 'a8-mini', 'ZR10') into a lookup key by lower-casing it and keeping only letters and digits, e.g. 'a8mini' or 'zr10'.

Returns the CameraProfile for a model name, optionally with changed fields: max_zoom > 0 replaces the maximum zoom (at least 1.0, and the optical part is cut to fit), photo_width / photo_height > 0 replace the photo size. An unknown name raises ValueError listing the valid names.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: when the emulator starts (SiyiEmulator.__init__)
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.inputs: name, max_zoom, photo_width, photo_height (the emulator parameters of the same names)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: A small zoom 'machine' that moves at a constant speed (zoom_speed_x_per_s, default 4x per second) between 1.0 and the model's maximum. It can travel to a target (command 0x0F) or zoom in/out until told to stop (command 0x05). It does not need a timer: it remembers where and when the last change started and works out the zoom for any moment you ask.
Sets up the zoom at 1.0x with the given maximum (never below 1.0), the travel speed (0 or less = instant) and the start time.
Keeps a zoom value inside 1.0 .. max_zoom.
Works out the zoom at time 'now': the starting zoom plus speed x elapsed time, but never past the target. With speed 0 or less it is simply the target.
The current zoom rounded to one decimal, which is how commands 0x05 and 0x18 report it.
Property: the zoom the lens is travelling to.
True while the zoom has not reached its target yet.
Command 0x0F (absolute zoom): starts travelling from the zoom right now towards the requested zoom, clamped to 1..max. Returns the clamped target.
Command 0x05 (manual zoom): direction 1 travels toward the maximum, -1 toward 1.0, and 0 stops right where it is. Returns the zoom at this moment.
Changes the upper zoom limit while keeping the current position and target inside the new limit.

The camera's changeable state besides the gimbal: its profile, strict mode (stay silent like a real A8 mini), whether the SD card is present, recording and HDR flags (no video is really recorded), mounting direction, video output setting and the ZoomState. It also builds the answer bytes for 0x01, 0x02 and 0x0A.
Runs right after the record is created: if no ZoomState was given it makes one with the profile's max zoom and zoom_speed_x_per_s.

True when the emulator must not answer this command: only in strict mode, and only for the commands a real A8 mini ignores over UDP (0x04 auto focus, 0x06 manual focus, 0x16 zoom range, 0x18 current zoom, 0x19 gimbal mode).
Property: byte 3 of the 0x0A answer: 0 idle, 1 recording, 2 'no TF card'. video_cam checks this byte to see whether the SD card is there.

Builds the answer to 0x0A (system info) in the layout video_cam reads: [0] 0, [1] HDR on/off, [2] 0, [3] record_sta, [4] gimbal mode (0 lock, 1 follow, 2 fpv), [5] mounting 1 normal / 2 inverted, [6] video output, [7] zoom linkage 0. It is cut to the model's length: 8 bytes for the ZR10, 7 for the A8 mini.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.inputs: the gimbal mode number from GimbalModel

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Builds the answer to 0x01: one 32-bit little-endian version word per firmware in the profile (3 words for the ZR10: camera, gimbal, zoom; 2 for the A8 mini).
Builds the answer to 0x02: the profile's 12-character hardware ID as ASCII bytes.

Command 0x0C function 2 (record): flips recording on or off and returns the 0x0B feedback code to push: 5 'record started' or 6 'record stopped'. Without an SD card nothing changes and it returns 4 'record failed'. No video file is ever written.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: Decides what the pretend camera does and answers for every SIYI SDK command. It takes one decoded frame, changes the camera state or the gimbal, and returns the reply frame, or nothing when a real camera would stay silent. Taking photos, pushing the 0x0B 'photo done' message and formatting the SD card are handed to 'hooks', so this file has no sockets, threads or Gazebo and can be tested on its own.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: SiyiEmulator._udp_loop (emulator.py) passes every frame that arrives on UDP 37260 from the team's video_cam driver to CommandHandler.handle and sends the reply back. Rules it copies from the real camera: replies echo the request's sequence number and use CTRL 0x02; 0x0C (photo) and 0x48 (format) are never answered; in strict mode 0x04/0x06/0x16/0x18/0x19 are not answered (like an A8 mini); unknown or broken commands are ignored with a one-time warning.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: The list of things the command handler needs from the rest of the emulator: the measured attitude, 'take a photo', 'push a 0x0B message' and 'format the SD card'. The default versions do nothing (no photo, attitude from the commanded joints, 0 files deleted), which is enough for unit tests; the emulator replaces them with _EmulatorHooks.
Remembers the gimbal model (optional) so the default attitude() can read its commanded joints.
Default attitude source: the attitude a camera would report for the gimbal's commanded joints, with zero rates; all zeros when there is no gimbal.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.outputs: (yaw, pitch, roll, yaw_rate, pitch_rate, roll_rate) in degrees and deg/s

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Placeholder for 'command 0x0C function 0 arrived: take a photo and later push 0x0B to this address'. The default does nothing.
Placeholder for 'send an unrequested 0x0B frame with this info_type to this address'. The default does nothing.
Placeholder for command 0x48: delete every photo and return how many files were deleted. The default deletes nothing and returns 0.

Turns SDK frames into state changes and replies. It holds the CameraState, the GimbalModel, the hooks, a lock shared with the emulator's control loop, a clock (replaceable in tests), a logger and a per-command counter, plus a table that maps each command number to the private method handling it.

Stores the camera, gimbal, hooks (default HandlerHooks), lock (a new RLock if none), clock (time.monotonic) and logger, and builds the dispatch table for the 19 known commands 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x04-0x08, 0x0A-0x0F, 0x16, 0x18, 0x19, 0x41 and 0x48.

Handles one frame: counts it, logs it (at INFO when log_commands is true), looks up its handler, and stays silent for unknown commands (one-time warning) or strict-mode silent ones. It runs the handler under the lock; a malformed payload is ignored with a one-time warning and any other error is logged, so nothing can crash the server. A result becomes a reply frame with the same sequence number and CTRL 0x02; for 0x41 the handler may pick a different reply command.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: for every frame that arrives on the SDK port (from video_cam, siyi_client or the tests)
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.inputs: a parsed Frame and the sender's (ip, port)
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.outputs: the reply Frame, or None for no answer

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Returns how many frames have been handled so far in total (read under the lock). Shown in the emulator's status.
Logs a warning only the first time a given key is seen, so a flood of the same bad command gives one line.
Logs an info message only the first time a given key is seen (shares the 'already said' set with _warn_once).
Gets the current yaw, pitch and roll from the hooks and packs them as the 6-byte angles payload used by the 0x0E and 0x41 replies.
Static helper: raises FrameError when a frame's payload is shorter than the number of bytes a command needs.
Command 0x00 (heartbeat, a TCP-only message): logs once that it was ignored and sends no reply, like the real camera does over UDP.
Command 0x01: answers with the firmware version words of the emulated model (CameraState.firmware_payload).
Command 0x02: answers with the 12-character hardware ID ('6B...' ZR10, '73...' A8 mini) that video_cam uses to detect the model.
Commands 0x04 (auto focus) and 0x06 (manual focus): the emulated lens is always sharp, so it just answers 01 (OK). In strict mode these never get here.
Command 0x05: reads the signed direction byte (1 zoom in, 0 stop, -1 zoom out), starts or stops the zoom travel, and answers with the zoom right now times ten as a 2-byte number.
Command 0x07 (gimbal speed): reads the yaw and pitch speeds (-100..100), starts the gimbal turning at that speed, and answers 01.
Command 0x08 (centre): data byte 2 or 4 points the camera straight down (yaw 0, pitch -90); anything else (normally 1) centres it to yaw 0, pitch 0. Answers 01.
Command 0x0A: answers with the system-info bytes, including record_sta (2 = no SD card) and the gimbal mode. video_cam sends this at start to check the SD card.
Command 0x0B: this message is something the CAMERA sends, so if a client sends it, it is ignored with no reply.

Command 0x0C, never answered directly. Function 0 = take a photo (hands it to hooks.take_photo; repeated sequence number 0 is fine). 1 toggles HDR, 2 toggles 'recording' (pushes 0x0B 'record failed' if there is no card), 3/4/5 switch the gimbal to lock/follow/FPV, 6/7/8 store a video-output setting, 9 points the camera straight down, 10 (zoom linkage) and unknown values are ignored with a one-time message.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: every photo the team's video_cam takes (it sends the fixed packet 55 66 01 01 00 00 00 0c 00 34 ce)
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.effects: starts a photo capture (Gazebo trigger, SD card file, 0x0B push) through the hooks

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Command 0x0D: answers with the 12-byte attitude (yaw, pitch, roll and their rates) from hooks.attitude(), which in the emulator uses the joint angles measured in Gazebo.
Command 0x0E: reads the requested yaw and pitch, packs the attitude BEFORE moving as the reply (like the real camera), then sets the new gimbal target (clamped to -135..135 yaw, -90..25 pitch).

Command 0x0F: reads the requested zoom (whole part, tenths), starts the zoom travelling there (clamped to the model's maximum, which is 1x on the A8 mini or with --zoom survey), logs once if it had to clamp, and answers 01. video_cam's capture_setup asks for 5.0x here.
Command 0x16: answers with the maximum zoom as (whole part, tenths).
Command 0x18: answers with the current zoom rounded to one decimal, as (whole part, tenths). video_cam polls this to confirm its zoom rack.
Command 0x19: answers with one byte, the gimbal mode (0 lock, 1 follow, 2 fpv).

Command 0x41: reads an angle and an axis (0 yaw, 1 pitch; anything else is treated as malformed), packs the attitude before moving, then changes only that axis. The reply's command number comes from the model profile: 0x41 on the ZR10 but 0x0E on the A8 mini, as on the real cameras.

Command 0x48 (format SD card): asks the hooks to delete every photo, logs how many files went, and sends no reply (the real camera does not answer either). The team's 'sd_format yes' command ends here; never use it on real hardware.
Formats a sender address as 'ip:port' for log lines, or '-' when there is none.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: The SIYI camera emulator itself, without ROS. It pretends to be the gimbal camera at 192.168.144.25 so the team's video_cam driver runs unchanged against Gazebo: UDP port 37260 receives and answers SIYI SDK commands (and pushes 0x0B 'photo OK'), TCP port 82 is the media web server for listing and downloading photos, and toward Gazebo it moves the gimbal joints 50 times a second (stabilised) and, on each 0x0C, asks the photo camera for one frame and writes it as a JPEG on the emulated SD card. Threads: 'siyi-udp', 'siyi-control', 'siyi-capture', the HTTP threads and Gazebo's callback threads; one lock guards the camera and gimbal state.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: This is the heart of the package: it ties together sdk_protocol, command_handler, camera_state, gimbal_control, gz_link, photo, sd_card, media_server and netutil. node.py wraps it as the ROS 2 node 'siyi_emulator' (started by the simulator's sim.launch.py); it can also run alone with 'python3 -m siyi_emulator.emulator --bind-ip 127.0.0.3 --no-gazebo'. Photo timing it is built around: video_cam waits 0.8 s for 0x0B, then polls the listing every 0.5 s for 15 s.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: The error raised when the emulator cannot start, e.g. a port is already used or port 82 is not allowed. Its message explains how to fix it (written by netutil.explain_bind_error).

Every setting of the emulator with its default and unit, as one record. Each field is also a ROS parameter of the same name: camera_model 'zr10', strict false, camera_ip 192.168.144.25, ctrl_port 37260, media_port 82, sd_card_dir ~/.ros/siyi_emulator/sd_card, photo_dir_name 101SIYI_IMG, jpeg_quality 92, photo_timeout_s 10, retrigger_after_s 3, feedback_deadline_s 0.5, initial_pitch_deg -90, control_rate_hz 50, the gz topic names, joint names, optical zoom settings and log_commands.
Class method: lists the names of all settings; node.py uses it to declare one ROS parameter per field.

Returns a copy of the settings with some values changed, converting each value to the type of its default (text 'true' becomes True, '3' becomes 3.0 for a float...). Also returns the names it did not know.
Builds the GzTopics record from the gz_*_topic settings, splitting optical_zoom_topics at commas.

Converts a text or number (from the command line or ROS) to a setting's type: booleans accept 1/true/yes/on and 0/false/no/off (anything else raises ValueError), ints go through float first ('2.0' -> 2), floats and strings are converted directly.

One waiting photo request: its number, the client address to push 0x0B to, when it was asked for, the 0x0B deadline timer, whether 0x0B was already sent, and a small lock so 0x0B goes out exactly once.
What photo listeners get after each saved photo: the PhotoFile and its metadata dict. The ROS node publishes it as JSON on /sim/camera/photo_info.
Connects the command handler's hooks to the running emulator: attitude -> current_attitude, take_photo -> request_photo, push_feedback -> push_feedback, format_sd -> the SD card's format.
Stores the emulator (and its gimbal, for the default hook behaviour).
Returns the emulator's current attitude (measured joints from Gazebo when fresh) for the 0x0D, 0x0E and 0x41 replies.
Passes a 0x0C 'take photo' to SiyiEmulator.request_photo with the client's address.
Passes a 0x0B push request to SiyiEmulator.push_feedback.
Formats the emulated SD card (deletes every photo) and returns how many files were deleted.

The running camera emulator: create it, start(), and later stop(). It owns the camera profile and state, the gimbal model, the SD card, the command handler, the Gazebo link (a fake one can be passed in by tests), the UDP socket, the media server, the photo job queue (at most 20 waiting), recent pose history (150 samples, about 3 s at 50 Hz, to match photos to poses) and counters for frames received/dropped/stale, timeouts and photos saved.

Builds everything from the config: the camera profile (get_profile), CameraState, GimbalLimits and GimbalModel (unknown initial_mode falls back to follow with a warning), the SdCard (cleared at start by default), the CommandHandler with _EmulatorHooks, and the Gazebo link (GzLink when use_gazebo is true, otherwise NullGzLink). Nothing is opened yet.
Property: the UDP SDK port really in use after start (37260 normally; tests use 0 = any free port).
Property: the TCP media port really in use after start (82 normally).

Opens everything: picks the listen address (resolve_bind_ip: 192.168.144.25 if this computer has it, else 127.0.0.1 with a warning), binds UDP 37260 and starts the media server on TCP 82 (a failure raises EmulatorStartError with the fix), connects the Gazebo callbacks and starts the Gazebo link (if that fails it warns that photos will be test patterns), starts the udp, control and capture threads, and logs 'SIYI camera emulator ready: ...' with model, address, ports, photo size and Gazebo status.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.effects: opens UDP 37260 and TCP 82 on the camera address; starts 3 threads; advertises/subscribes the Gazebo topics

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Stops all threads (waiting up to 2 s each), closes the UDP socket, stops the media server and drops the Gazebo link. Safe to call twice.
Waits (checking every 0.5 s) until stop() is called; used by the stand-alone command line.
Logs a warning only the first time a given key appears, so repeated problems give one line.
Sends bytes over the UDP socket to a client address; a send error is warned about once per address and never crashes anything.

The 'siyi-udp' thread: waits for UDP packets (0.5 s timeout so it can notice stop), logs each new client once ('SDK client ... connected'), splits the packet into frames (bad bytes give one-time warnings), hands each frame to CommandHandler.handle and sends any reply straight back to the sender.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: runs for the emulator's whole life; one turn per packet from video_cam or siyi_client

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Sends an unrequested 0x0B 'function feedback' frame to a client: info_type 0 = photo OK, 1 = photo failed (no TF card), 4 = record failed. Each push gets its own sequence number and CTRL 0x02.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.effects: UDP frame to video_cam, which waits up to 0.8 s for it after each 0x0C

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Remembers the newest Gazebo sim time seen in any message; used to throw away photo frames older than the current trigger.
Gazebo callback: stores the latest drone odometry sample and adds it to the pose history (under the lock).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: every /sim/drone/odometry message (gz-transport thread)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Gazebo callback: stores the latest measured gimbal joints and adds them to the joint history (under the lock).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: every /sim/gimbal/joint_states message

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Gazebo callback: keeps the latest photo-camera lens data (width and focal length) for the field of view in the metadata.

Gazebo callback for each rendered photo frame: counts it, and if the capture worker is waiting and the frame is not older than the trigger, hands it over and wakes the worker. Frames nobody waits for are dropped (with a one-time warning if one arrives after its photo already timed out: 'raise photo_timeout_s'); old frames from an earlier trigger are dropped as stale.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: every /sim/camera/photo/image frame

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Returns the measured joint angles from Gazebo if they are at most 1 s old and have all three axes, otherwise None (then the commanded angles are used).

Gives (yaw, pitch, roll) in degrees the way the real camera reports them, plus their smoothed rates in deg/s. It uses the measured Gazebo joints when fresh, else the commanded joints, through GimbalModel.reported_attitude.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: for 0x0D/0x0E/0x41 replies, every control-loop turn (rates) and for the status

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Estimates how fast the reported yaw, pitch and roll change: the difference since the last turn divided by the time, lightly smoothed (30 % new, 70 % old). These are the rates in the 0x0D reply.

The 'siyi-control' thread, about 50 times a second (control_rate_hz): feeds the drone attitude from odometry into the gimbal, steps the gimbal (slew limit + stabilisation), publishes the three joint targets to Gazebo, updates the attitude rates, sends the CameraZoomPlugin command when optical zoom is on (on change and again every second), and runs the health checks. Any error is warned about once and the loop keeps going.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.effects: gz /sim/gimbal/yaw|roll|pitch/cmd_pos at 50 Hz; optional optical zoom topics

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: From 15 s after start, warns once if no drone odometry has arrived (the camera is then stabilised as if the drone were level; check the drone is spawned, its OdometryPublisher topic and GZ_PARTITION) or no gimbal joint states (0x0D then reports commanded angles).

Handles 0x0C 'take photo' without blocking: with no SD card it pushes 0x0B 'photo failed' at once; otherwise it queues a capture job and arms a timer that pushes 0x0B 'photo OK' after feedback_deadline_s (0.5 s) at the latest, so video_cam (which waits 0.8 s) never times out. If 20 photos are already waiting it refuses with 'photo failed'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: each 0x0C function 0 from video_cam (about once a second during the survey)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Pushes a job's 0x0B message exactly once (the deadline timer and the worker may both try; a small lock decides) and cancels the timer.
The 'siyi-capture' thread: takes photo jobs from the queue one at a time and runs _process_job; if a job crashes it logs the error and pushes 0x0B 'photo failed'.

Gets one rendered frame from Gazebo: publishes the trigger on /sim/camera/photo/trigger, waits for _on_photo to hand over a frame, re-sends the trigger after retrigger_after_s (3 s) up to 2 more times, and gives up after photo_timeout_s (10 s) with a warning (adding 'nothing listens to the trigger topic' when Gazebo says so). Without a Gazebo link it returns at once.

Makes one photo: gets a Gazebo frame (pushing 0x0B 'photo OK' as soon as it arrives), converts it to a picture (resizing with a one-time warning if Gazebo's size differs from the model's), or, if there is no frame, saves a labelled test pattern (or loses the photo and pushes 'photo failed' when test_pattern_fallback is false). Then it applies the digital part of the current zoom, encodes the JPEG, builds the metadata, writes IMG_NNNN.jpg (+ .json) to the SD card, logs 'photo IMG_NNNN.jpg saved ...' and tells the photo listeners.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.effects: writes the photo to the SD card folder; the ROS node then publishes /sim/camera/photo_info

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Static helper: from a history of time-stamped samples, picks the one whose sim time is closest to a photo's time stamp; falls back to the latest sample when there is no stamp or history.

Builds the photo's metadata dict (saved as IMG_NNNN.json and published on /sim/camera/photo_info): emulator and model name, wall and sim time, trigger-to-frame delay, image size and source (gazebo or test_pattern), zoom (total/optical/digital), lens and effective field of view, gimbal mode, yaw joint angle and pitch/roll against the horizon (gimbal_earth_angles, from the measured joints closest in time, else the commanded ones), drone position and orientation from the odometry closest in time, and the camera's world position, look direction, optical quaternion, compass heading and pitch.

A JSON-friendly snapshot of the emulator: model, strict flag, address and ports, Gazebo link status, odometry and joint-state ages, gimbal mode and attitude, zoom (current, target, max), photos saved and on the card, photo-frame counters (received, dropped, stale, timeouts), last photo, SD folder, number of clients and commands received.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: 2 times a second by the ROS node for /sim/camera/emulator_state

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Defines the stand-alone command-line options: --camera-model, --strict, --camera-ip, --bind-ip, --ctrl-port, --media-port, --sd-card-dir, --no-gazebo, --params-file (a ROS-style YAML), --param NAME=VALUE (any setting, repeatable) and --log-level.

Builds an EmulatorConfig from the parsed command line in the order: YAML params file, then the flags, then each --param NAME=VALUE (last wins). A --param without '=' or an unknown setting name stops the program with a message listing the valid names.

Runs the emulator without ROS until Ctrl-C or SIGTERM: parses the options, sets up logging, creates and starts SiyiEmulator (exit code 2 with the reason if it cannot start), waits, then stops it. Returns 0 normally.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: python3 -m siyi_emulator.emulator ... (node.py also uses it for the --no-ros mode)

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: The 'brain' of the pretend 3-axis gimbal (the motorised camera mount). It turns SIYI gimbal commands (0x0E set angles, 0x41 one axis, 0x07 speed, 0x08 centre, lock/follow/FPV mode) into the three joint angles (yaw, roll, pitch) Gazebo must turn the gimbal to. It keeps the camera level when the drone tilts (stabilisation, using the drone attitude from /sim/drone/odometry), limits turning to about 90 deg per second, and works out the attitude a real camera would report for 0x0D. Uses numpy math only, no ROS.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: emulator.py owns one GimbalModel: command_handler.py changes its targets when video_cam sends a gimbal command, the emulator's 50 Hz control loop calls step() and sends the joint targets to Gazebo on /sim/gimbal/yaw|roll|pitch/cmd_pos, and the photo metadata (camera position and look direction in each IMG_NNNN.json and on /sim/camera/photo_info) is computed with camera_world_pose. Sign rules: joint yaw + = camera turns LEFT, pitch -90 deg = straight down; SIYI speeds (0x07) use yaw + = RIGHT.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Makes the 3x3 rotation matrix for turning by an angle (radians) around the X axis.
Makes the 3x3 rotation matrix for turning by an angle (radians) around the Y axis.
Makes the 3x3 rotation matrix for turning by an angle (radians) around the Z axis.
Makes a rotation matrix from roll, pitch and yaw (radians) the way SDF/URDF robot files do: first roll about X, then pitch about Y, then yaw about Z (R = Rz(yaw) Ry(pitch) Rx(roll)).

Turns a quaternion (x, y, z, w), the 4-number way Gazebo reports an orientation, into a 3x3 rotation matrix. It normalises the quaternion first; an all-zero quaternion gives 'no rotation' (the identity matrix).
Turns a 3x3 rotation matrix back into a unit quaternion (x, y, z, w) using Shepperd's method, which picks the numerically safest formula. Used for the optical-frame orientation in the photo metadata.

Splits a rotation matrix into (roll, pitch, yaw) radians so that R = Rz(yaw) Ry(pitch) Rx(roll). When the frame points straight up or down it puts all the turning into yaw. Careful: here a positive pitch means nose DOWN; camera_heading_pitch_roll flips it to SIYI style.
Wraps an angle in degrees into the range -180 up to (but not including) 180, e.g. 190 -> -170.
Converts a Gazebo heading (radians, counter-clockwise from east) into a compass bearing (degrees clockwise from north, 0..360). Example: 90 deg ENU (north) -> 0 deg compass.
A small named tuple of the three gimbal joint angles in radians, always in chain order (yaw, roll, pitch).
Forward kinematics: given the joint angles, gives the camera's rotation relative to the drone body, R = Rz(yaw) Rx(roll) Ry(-pitch) (the pitch joint turns about -Y, so + pitch tilts up).

Inverse kinematics: given the rotation the camera should have relative to the drone, finds the yaw, roll and pitch joint angles that produce it (the reverse of body_to_camera, using asin/atan2 on matrix entries). The impossible case (roll exactly +-90 deg) is far outside the +-30 deg roll range.

FPV mode: finds joint angles that point the camera at a given world heading and elevation while keeping the roll joint at zero, so the picture's horizon tilts with the drone (that is what FPV mode does).

Reads a camera's rotation in the world and returns (heading, pitch, roll) in radians: heading = which way it looks (ENU yaw), pitch = elevation with + = up (SIYI style), roll = turn about the look direction with + = right side down. It uses the Z-Y-X split, which gets shaky exactly at pitch -90 (straight down), so the reported gimbal angles now use gimbal_earth_angles instead; camera_world_pose still uses this one for the camera's world heading and pitch.

Splits a camera's rotation in the world into (heading, roll, pitch) radians in the gimbal's own motor order yaw -> roll -> pitch (R = Rz(heading) Rx(roll) Ry(-pitch), solved with solve_joints). Pitch + = up, -90 = straight down, and it carries on smoothly past -90; roll + = right side down. Added on 2026-10-31 because the older Z-Y-X split reported a random roll (photo sidecars showed -177.7 to +176.4 deg) when the camera was a few tenths of a degree off straight down, the survey pose.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: for every 0x0D/0x0E/0x41 attitude reply (GimbalModel.reported_attitude) and for each photo's gimbal pitch/roll in the metadata (SiyiEmulator._photo_metadata)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Works out where the camera lens sits in the drone body frame (metres) for given joint angles, by chaining the small offsets of the A8 mini's joints from its URDF onto the mount point under the nose (0.07, 0, -0.06 m). Only used for photo metadata (a few centimetres).

A record of where the camera is and where it looks in the Gazebo world (ENU): position in metres, the x-forward camera rotation, the optical-frame rotation (z forward, x right, y down), and heading, pitch and roll in radians.
Property: the unit vector the camera is looking along in the world (the first column of its rotation matrix).
Property: the optical frame's orientation as an (x, y, z, w) quaternion (via quat_from_rot).
Property: the compass bearing of the look direction in degrees clockwise from north.

Forward kinematics all the way to the world: from the drone's position and rotation plus the joint angles it computes the camera's world position, its two rotations and its heading/pitch/roll, and returns them as a CameraWorldPose.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: for every saved photo, when the emulator writes the photo metadata

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: The gimbal's limits in degrees. Commandable limits (what 0x0E/0x41/0x07 may ask for, clamped like the hardware): yaw -135..135, pitch -90..25. Mechanical joint limits (wider, so stabilisation still works near the edge): yaw +-160, roll +-30, pitch -135..+45.
Keeps a commanded yaw (deg) inside the commandable range.
Keeps a commanded pitch (deg) inside the commandable range.
Keeps joint angles (radians) inside the mechanical limits before they are sent to Gazebo.

The gimbal's state machine: it stores a target (where the user wants the camera to point) and a command angle that follows the target at no more than max_slew_dps (90 deg/s). In follow and FPV mode the yaw is relative to the drone; in lock mode it is a world heading, so the camera keeps pointing the same way when the drone turns. A 0x07 speed command keeps moving the target every step. It is not thread-safe, so the emulator holds a lock around it.

Sets up the gimbal from the emulator parameters: limits, max_slew_dps, rate_yaw_sign (-1 turns a SIYI 'right' speed into the + = left angle frame), max_rate_dps, initial mode (follow by default), stabilize, initial yaw/pitch (the emulator starts at pitch -90 = straight down) and the mount position. It then computes the first joint targets.
Feeds in the drone's latest orientation as a quaternion (x, y, z, w) from /sim/drone/odometry; converts it to a matrix and passes it to set_drone_rotation.
Stores the drone's latest orientation matrix and its heading in degrees (counter-clockwise from east). Stabilisation and lock mode use these.
Property: the latest drone orientation matrix ('no rotation' until odometry arrives).
Property: the drone's heading in ENU degrees (counter-clockwise from east).
Converts a stored yaw into 'degrees relative to the drone': in lock mode it subtracts the drone heading (wrapped to +-180); in the other modes the value is already relative.
The reverse of _to_relative: turns a yaw relative to the drone into the stored form (in lock mode it adds the drone heading, so it becomes a world heading).
Property: the yaw the gimbal is commanded to right now, relative to the drone (SIYI degrees, + = left).
Property: the yaw target relative to the drone (SIYI degrees, + = left).
Switches between 0 lock, 1 follow and 2 FPV. The stored yaw values are converted to the new mode's frame so the camera does not jump. Any other number raises ValueError.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: 0x0C functions 3/4/5 (lock/follow/fpv) from video_cam or siyi_client

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Command 0x0E: sets new yaw and pitch targets in SIYI degrees (yaw + = left, pitch + = up), clamped to the commandable range, and stops any running speed command. Returns the clamped (yaw, pitch). video_cam's gimbal_set_angles 0,-90 lands here.
Command 0x41 with axis 0: changes only the yaw target (clamped) and stops a yaw speed command. Returns the clamped yaw.
Command 0x41 with axis 1: changes only the pitch target (clamped) and stops a pitch speed command. Returns the clamped pitch.
Command 0x08 (one-key centre): points the camera straight ahead, yaw 0 and pitch 0.
Sets turning speeds already in the angle frame (yaw + = left, pitch + = up) in deg/s; 0, 0 stops.

Command 0x07 (gimbal speed): takes SIYI speeds -100..100 (yaw + = RIGHT, pitch + = up), converts them to deg/s (100 = max_rate_dps, 90 deg/s) with rate_yaw_sign flipping the yaw, and starts turning. Returns the speeds used.
Property: True while a 0x07 speed command is moving the gimbal.

Moves time forward by dt seconds (capped at 0.5 s): a running speed command moves the targets, then the command angles move toward the targets by at most 90 deg/s x dt (lock-mode yaw wraps the short way round). Finally it solves the joint angles and returns them.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: about 50 times a second by the emulator's control loop (control_rate_hz)
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.outputs: Joints (yaw, roll, pitch) in radians for Gazebo

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Inverse kinematics for the current command angles: without stabilisation the joints are just the commanded yaw and pitch; with it, it computes a level-horizon camera rotation in the world (heading = drone heading + yaw, given pitch, zero roll) and solves the joints that cancel the drone's tilt. FPV mode uses solve_joints_fpv instead. The result is clamped to the mechanical limits.

Works out what a real SIYI camera would report in 0x0D/0x0E from the measured joint angles: yaw = the yaw joint itself (relative to the drone, like the A8's magnetic encoder); pitch and roll relative to the horizon (like its camera IMU) when stabilising, split in the gimbal's own yaw -> roll -> pitch order by gimbal_earth_angles, so a camera held straight down reads pitch -90 / roll 0 steadily; without stabilisation the raw joint angles.
Returns the camera's world pose for a drone position and joint angles, using the latest drone attitude and the mount position (calls camera_world_pose).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: The emulator's only wire to Gazebo, using Gazebo's own Python messaging library (gz-transport 13 + gz-msgs 10; no ROS bridge needed). It sends the gimbal joint targets and the 'take one photo' trigger, and listens to the measured joint angles, the drone's odometry, the rendered photo and the photo camera's lens data. Everything received is handed on as small plain-Python records, so the rest of the emulator never touches Gazebo's message types. NullGzLink is a do-nothing stand-in with the same buttons.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: Created by SiyiEmulator (emulator.py) when use_gazebo is true. Gazebo topics (gz-transport, not ROS): publishes /sim/gimbal/yaw|roll|pitch/cmd_pos (gz.msgs.Double, radians) and /sim/camera/photo/trigger (gz.msgs.Boolean); subscribes /sim/gimbal/joint_states (gz.msgs.Model), /sim/drone/odometry (gz.msgs.Odometry), /sim/camera/photo/image (gz.msgs.Image) and /sim/camera/photo/camera_info. The drone model from sim_models (iris_a8mini) provides the other end of these topics.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Every Gazebo topic name the emulator uses, with the simulation contract's names as defaults: /sim/gimbal/yaw|roll|pitch/cmd_pos, /sim/gimbal/joint_states, /sim/drone/odometry, /sim/camera/photo/image, /sim/camera/photo/camera_info, /sim/camera/photo/trigger, and an optional list of CameraZoomPlugin topics (empty by default).
One drone pose from /sim/drone/odometry: Gazebo sim time (or None), position in metres (ENU: x east, y north, z up), orientation quaternion (x, y, z, w) and the local time it arrived.
One reading of the measured gimbal joints: angles and speeds keyed 'yaw', 'roll', 'pitch' (radians, rad/s), the sim time and the local arrival time.
One rendered photo frame still as raw bytes (width, height, bytes per row, pixel format, data, sim time, arrival time). It is converted to an OpenCV picture later, off Gazebo's thread.
Lens data of the photo camera: image width and height and focal length fx in pixels (used to compute the true field of view for the photo metadata).
Reads the sim time in seconds (sec + nsec x 1e-9) from a Gazebo message header, or None when the message has no time stamp.

Finds which joint in a Gazebo joint_states message is our yaw, roll and pitch joint. A wanted name like 'gimbal_yaw' matches exactly, or as the end of a scoped name ('iris::gimbal_yaw', 'model/gimbal_yaw'), or as a last resort anywhere inside a name; roles that match nothing are left out.

A Gazebo link that does nothing (available = False), with the same methods and callback slots as GzLink. The emulator uses it when use_gazebo is false, and the tests pass it (or their FakeGzLink, which is built on it) in. GzLink is built on it too, so a GzLink whose start() failed (for example because the Gazebo Python bindings are missing) behaves the same way. Photos then become test patterns (with the default test_pattern_fallback).
Stores why there is no Gazebo (the reason text shown in the status), empty callback slots (on_odometry, on_joint_states, on_photo, on_camera_info) and a trigger counter.
Nothing to start; returns False (not connected).
Nothing to stop.
Ignores gimbal joint targets (there is no Gazebo to send them to).
Counts the trigger but sends nothing and returns False, meaning no frame will come.
Ignores optical zoom commands.
Returns None: without Gazebo nobody can tell whether a photo camera is listening.

The real gz-transport connection. It holds the topic names, the joint names from the drone SDF (gimbal_yaw, gimbal_roll, gimbal_pitch by default), an optional GZ_PARTITION and the Gazebo publishers. Callbacks set by the emulator run on gz-transport's own threads, so they are kept short.
Stores the topics, joint names, partition and logger; marks itself 'not started'. Nothing connects until start().

Imports the Gazebo Python bindings (if missing it sets a reason telling you to install python3-gz-transport13 and python3-gz-msgs10, or to run with use_gazebo:=false, and returns False). It sets GZ_PARTITION if one was given, creates a gz Node, advertises the three gimbal command topics and the photo trigger (plus any zoom topics), subscribes to odometry, joint states, the photo image and camera_info, and logs 'Gazebo link up ...'. Returns True when connected.
Drops the gz Node and publishers and marks the link unavailable (gz-transport cleans up its own threads).
Sends the three gimbal joint targets (radians) as gz.msgs.Double on /sim/gimbal/yaw/cmd_pos, /roll/cmd_pos and /pitch/cmd_pos, where the drone model's joint position controllers pick them up.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: about 50 times a second from the emulator's control loop

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Publishes one gz.msgs.Boolean (true) on /sim/camera/photo/trigger, which makes the drone's triggered photo camera render exactly ONE frame. Counts the trigger and returns True when the message went out.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: once per photo request, and again (at most twice more) if no frame came within retrigger_after_s (3 s)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Sends a CameraZoomPlugin command (a gz.msgs.Double, see photo.zoom_plugin_command) to every configured optical zoom topic. Only used when optical_zoom_topics is set.

Asks gz-transport whether anything (the drone's photo camera) listens to the trigger topic /sim/camera/photo/trigger: True or False, or None when it cannot tell. The emulator only asks after a photo frame did not arrive in time (SiyiEmulator._acquire_frame), to add 'and nothing listens to the trigger topic (is the drone spawned?)' to its warning.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: after a photo frame did not arrive within photo_timeout_s (10 s)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Gazebo callback for /sim/drone/odometry: copies position and orientation into an OdomSample and hands it to the emulator's on_odometry callback.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: every odometry message from the drone's OdometryPublisher

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Gazebo callback for /sim/gimbal/joint_states: finds (once, or again when names change) which joints are yaw/roll/pitch with match_joint_names, warns once if one is missing (then commanded angles are used instead), and hands the measured angles and speeds to on_joint_states as a JointSample.
Gazebo callback for /sim/camera/photo/image: wraps the rendered frame's size, row length, pixel format and bytes in a RawImage and hands it to the emulator's on_photo callback.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: each time the triggered photo camera renders a frame

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Gazebo callback for /sim/camera/photo/camera_info: reads the image size and the focal length fx (first entry of the intrinsics matrix, 0 if missing) and hands a CameraInfoSample to on_camera_info.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: The pretend camera's little web server on TCP port 82, the same one the real SIYI camera has. After the shutter fires, the team's video_cam driver uses it to find the newest photo and download it. It answers exactly the requests and JSON shapes video_cam depends on: getdirectories, getmedialist (oldest first), getmediacount, the photo files themselves, plus a small HTML page at / for people with a browser. Standard library only (http.server).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.effects: opens a TCP listening socket on bind_ip:82 (needs net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=80)
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: Serves the emulated SD card (sd_card.py) started by emulator.py. video_cam polls http://192.168.144.25:82/cgi-bin/media.cgi/api/v1/getmedialist?media_type=0&path=101SIYI_IMG&start=0&count=9999 every 0.5 s (up to 15 s), then GETs the photo URL. Each photo URL uses the Host header the client used, so the link always works for that client.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Builds the SIYI media API reply 'envelope': {code, data, success, message}. Success replies use code 200 and an empty message.
Turns a query-string value into a whole number, or returns the given default when it is missing or not a number.
Reads the media_type query value: '0' = images, '1' = videos, missing = images, anything else = None (invalid).
Builds the getdirectories answer: the one photo folder [{name: '101SIYI_IMG', path: '101SIYI_IMG'}] for images, an empty list for videos, or a code-400 'Invalid media type' error.

Builds the getmedialist answer: for our folder, the photos oldest first, cut by start and count, each with name, full download URL (base_url + '/101SIYI_IMG/IMG_NNNN.jpg') and size, plus 'total' = all photos. Wrong media type gives code 400 'Invalid media type', a wrong folder gives 400 'path not exist', videos give an empty list.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.inputs: the SdCard, media type, folder path, start, count (video_cam asks 9999, or 1 to read the total), base URL 'http://host:port'

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Builds the getmediacount answer {count: N} for our photo folder (0 for videos), with the same 400 errors as getmedialist.

Makes the small HTML page shown at http://192.168.144.25:82/: the folder name, where it is on this computer, every photo newest first with its size in MB as a download link, and links to the two API calls.

The threaded HTTP server for the SD card: it knows the card, the listen address (e.g. 192.168.144.25 or 127.0.0.1), the port (82; 0 = any free port in tests), an optional fixed host for photo URLs (media_url_host), a logger and a request counter.
Stores the SD card, listen address, requested port, URL host and logger; the server itself is created later by start().
Property: the TCP port really in use (useful in tests that asked for port 0).

Creates the HTTP server on bind_ip:port with the handler class from _make_handler and runs it in a background thread named 'siyi-media-http'. Raises OSError when the port cannot be used (busy, or port 82 not allowed for normal users).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.effects: opens the TCP listening socket; one thread per client connection

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Stops serving, closes the socket and waits up to 2 s for the thread; safe to call twice.
Builds 'http://host[:port]' for photo URLs: the media_url_host parameter if set, otherwise the request's Host header, otherwise the listen address and port.

Builds the request-handler class tied to one MediaServer (Python's http.server wants a class, not an object). The class speaks HTTP/1.1 keep-alive (what video_cam's requests.Session likes) and closes idle connections after 120 s.

The per-request handler class built by _make_handler. It routes GET and HEAD requests: API calls under /cgi-bin/media.cgi/api/v1/, the index page at / or /index.html, and everything else as a file on the card.
Sends http.server's own access-log lines to the emulator's logger at DEBUG level instead of printing them.
Answers a GET request (with a body) by calling _handle.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: every HTTP GET from video_cam (listing polls every 0.5 s, then the photo download) or a browser

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Answers a HEAD request: the same headers as GET but no body.
Sends one reply: status code, Content-Type and Content-Length headers, then the body (left out for HEAD).
Sends a dict as a JSON reply with status 200 (SIYI puts errors inside the JSON, not in the HTTP status).

Main request router: counts the request, cleans the path (decodes it and turns double slashes into one, so SIYI's documented 'http://host:82//cgi-bin/...' works), reads the query string, then calls _handle_api, sends the index page, or calls _handle_file. A client that hangs up is ignored; any other error is logged and answered with 500, so one bad request never kills the server.
Answers the three API calls getdirectories, getmedialist and getmediacount with the JSON builders above (start defaults to 0, count to 'everything'); an unknown API name gets a code-404 JSON error.
Serves one file from the card, e.g. /101SIYI_IMG/IMG_0001.jpg, as image/jpeg (.json as application/json); a path outside the card or a missing file gets 404 'not found'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.effects: this is the download video_cam saves as '<lat> , <lon>.jpg' in mapping_photos

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: Decides which IP address the emulator listens on, and turns network errors into fix-it sentences. The team's video_cam talks to the camera at 192.168.144.25, so the emulator can only answer there if this computer owns that address (scripts/add_camera_ip.sh adds it to the loopback interface). Rules: a given bind_ip is used as is; otherwise 192.168.144.25 if it exists here; otherwise 127.0.0.1 with a warning. Standard library only.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: Called by SiyiEmulator.start (emulator.py) before it opens UDP 37260 and TCP 82. Its messages are what you see when the camera address alias is missing, port 82 is not allowed, or another emulator (maybe in the other WSL distro) already holds the ports.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Checks whether an IP address belongs to this computer by trying to bind a throw-away UDP socket to it on port 0: the operating system refuses addresses it does not own. No root needed, nothing is sent.

Picks the listen address: a non-empty bind_ip as given; else the camera_ip (192.168.144.25) if it exists on this computer; else 127.0.0.1 plus a warning sentence saying video_cam then needs '-p camera_ip:=127.0.0.1', or that you can add the address with add_camera_ip.sh.

Turns a failed bind into a sentence that says how to fix it: 'no permission' on a port below 1024 -> run 'sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=80'; 'address in use' -> another emulator or the other WSL distro has it, stop it or use bind_ip 127.0.0.3; 'address not available' -> run scripts/add_camera_ip.sh or set bind_ip:=127.0.0.1; anything else -> the raw error.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: The ROS 2 front door of the camera emulator (the executable 'siyi_emulator'). It declares one ROS parameter per emulator setting (same names as EmulatorConfig, each with a short description for 'ros2 param describe'), starts the emulator core, forwards its log lines to the ROS logger, and publishes two simulator-only JSON topics. If ROS is missing, or with --standalone / --no-ros, the same program runs emulator.py's plain command line instead.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: Started by the simulator's launch (sim.launch.py, or launch/siyi_emulator.launch.py) as node 'siyi_emulator'. The emulator talks to video_cam over UDP/HTTP and to Gazebo over gz-transport, not ROS; ROS is only used for the extras /sim/camera/photo_info (one JSON per saved photo, RELIABLE + TRANSIENT_LOCAL, depth 10; read by sim_demo's score_run, demo_markers and truth_detector) and /sim/camera/emulator_state (JSON status at publish_state_hz, default 2 Hz).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Returns the argument list without the given flags (used to remove --standalone / --no-ros before passing the rest on).

Entry point of 'ros2 run siyi_emulator siyi_emulator'. With --standalone or --no-ros it runs the plain emulator command line (emulator.main); if rclpy cannot be imported it says so and does the same; otherwise it runs the ROS node through _run_ros.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.outputs: the process exit code (0 ok, 2 could not start)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Starts ROS (rclpy.init), builds the emulator node, and spins it until Ctrl-C or shutdown, then stops the emulator and closes ROS cleanly. If the emulator cannot start (port in use, unknown camera_model ...) it logs a FATAL 'cannot start the SIYI emulator: ...' and returns 2.

A Python logging handler that forwards the emulator core's log lines to the ROS logger at the matching level (error, warning, info, debug), prefixing lines from child loggers with their short name, e.g. '[sdk] ...' or '[gz] ...'. It never raises.
Remembers the ROS logger to forward to.
Sends one log record to the ROS logger with the right severity (ERROR and above -> error, WARNING -> warning, INFO -> info, lower -> debug).

Imports the ROS pieces (Node, QoS, std_msgs String, ParameterDescriptor) only when needed, defines the SiyiEmulatorNode class and returns one instance. Keeping it in a function lets the module load without ROS.
The ROS 2 node 'siyi_emulator': ROS parameters -> EmulatorConfig -> a running SiyiEmulator, plus the two JSON publishers.

Declares every emulator parameter plus publish_photo_info, photo_info_topic, publish_state_hz and state_topic, with dynamic typing so '-p initial_pitch_deg:=-90' (an integer) is accepted and converted. It builds the config, routes the 'siyi_emulator' Python logger into ROS (DEBUG if the ROS logger is at debug), creates the emulator, creates the photo_info publisher (RELIABLE, TRANSIENT_LOCAL, depth 10) and registers it as a photo listener, starts the emulator (raises EmulatorStartError with a helpful message if a port fails), and starts the state timer.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.effects: opens UDP 37260 / TCP 82 through the emulator; creates the /sim/camera/photo_info and /sim/camera/emulator_state publishers

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Photo listener: publishes one JSON message on /sim/camera/photo_info for each saved photo: the photo metadata plus sd_name, sd_path, size_bytes and its URL http://<camera_ip>:82/101SIYI_IMG/IMG_NNNN.jpg.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: after every photo the emulator saves (about once a second during a survey)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Timer callback: publishes SiyiEmulator.status() as JSON on /sim/camera/emulator_state (2 times a second by default). 'ros2 topic echo --full-length /sim/camera/emulator_state' shows the emulator's health.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: every 1/publish_state_hz seconds (0.5 s by default)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Stops the emulator (threads, sockets, Gazebo link) before the node is destroyed.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: Turns one picture rendered by Gazebo into the JPEG the camera stores on its SD card. It converts Gazebo's raw image bytes into an OpenCV picture, applies the digital zoom (cut out the centre and stretch it back to full size, which is all a digital zoom is), encodes the JPEG (quality 92 by default), draws a clearly labelled test pattern when Gazebo sends no picture, and holds the zoom and field-of-view maths, including the number to send to ardupilot_gazebo's CameraZoomPlugin for real optical zoom. numpy + OpenCV, no ROS.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: SiyiEmulator._process_job (emulator.py) calls these helpers for every photo between 'frame arrived on gz /sim/camera/photo/image' and 'IMG_NNNN.jpg written to the SD card'. The field-of-view numbers also go into the photo metadata (IMG_NNNN.json and /sim/camera/photo_info).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Raises a clear RuntimeError ('OpenCV (python3-opencv) is required to make photos') when OpenCV could not be imported; the rest of the emulator still loads without it.

Converts the fields of a Gazebo image message (width, height, bytes per row, raw bytes, pixel format) into an OpenCV colour picture in BGR order (height x width x 3). It understands grey (L8), RGB (format 3, what Gazebo cameras send), BGR, RGBA and BGRA; an unknown format or too few bytes raises ValueError.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: for each Gazebo photo frame taken for a capture

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Works out the centre rectangle (x0, y0, width, height) to keep for a digital zoom factor: the picture size divided by the zoom, rounded to even numbers and at least 2x2 pixels. Example: 2560x1440 at 2x keeps the middle 1280x720.
Does the digital zoom: keeps the centre 1/zoom of the picture (crop_rect) and resizes it to the output size. With zoom 1.0 and the same size it returns the picture untouched.
Splits a total zoom into (optical, digital) parts: the optical part goes up to the given optical limit and the rest is digital. Example: 15x with a 10x optical limit -> (10, 1.5).
Gives the horizontal field of view (radians) after zooming: 2 x atan(tan(hfov/2) / zoom). This is true for both cropping and real optics. Example: 81 deg at 5x -> about 19.4 deg.

Gives the number to publish to ardupilot_gazebo's CameraZoomPlugin for a real optical zoom. The plugin sets the field of view to 2.0 rad divided by the command (a fixed 2.0, not the camera's own field of view), so this sends 2.0 / zoomed_hfov(...) to get the physically right view. Example: hfov 1.4137 rad, zoom 1 -> 1.4147; zoom 5 -> 5.910.
Works out the horizontal field of view in radians from Gazebo's camera_info (image width and focal length fx in pixels): 2 x atan(width / (2 fx)). Returns None for zero or negative inputs.
Encodes a BGR picture as JPEG bytes with OpenCV at the given quality (kept inside 1..100); raises RuntimeError if encoding fails.

Draws the stand-in picture used when Gazebo sends no photo: random coloured noise, a white grid, a red circle in the middle and big yellow text 'SIYI EMULATOR TEST PATTERN', 'NO GAZEBO PHOTO FRAME' plus extra lines (the emulator adds the photo number and the reason). It is obviously not a real view but decodes like any photo and stays above video_cam's minimum JPEG size (50 kB for the 4K profile).

Resizes a picture to (width, height) if it is not already that size (shrinking uses INTER_AREA, growing INTER_LINEAR) and returns the same picture when the size already matches. The emulator itself never calls it (only test_photo.py does): a Gazebo frame of the wrong size is scaled by apply_digital_zoom, which always resizes the crop to the photo size.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: The pretend camera's micro SD ('TF') card. Photos are real JPEG files in ONE folder on the computer: <sd_card_dir>/101SIYI_IMG/IMG_0001.jpg, plus IMG_0001.json with the photo's metadata. It numbers the photos, writes them safely (temp file + rename, so nobody ever reads half a JPEG), lists them oldest first, finds files for downloads without letting a URL escape the card folder, and deletes everything on a format. Thread-safe.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: emulator.py writes every finished photo here; media_server.py lists and serves these files over HTTP port 82 to the team's video_cam driver. There is one folder for the whole run because video_cam only watches the last directory it was told about. Default folder ~/.ros/siyi_emulator/sd_card (parameter sd_card_dir); AGENTS.md says the full simulator uses ~/.astra_sim/sd_card_I<I>.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: A read-only record of one photo on the card: its number (the NNNN of IMG_NNNN.jpg), file name, full path, size in bytes, and rel_path '101SIYI_IMG/IMG_NNNN.jpg' (the path part of its download URL).
Turns the sd_card_dir parameter into a full path: expands '~' and $VARIABLES; an empty value means ~/.ros/siyi_emulator/sd_card.

The folder-backed SD card. It keeps the card root, the single photo directory name (default '101SIYI_IMG'), the next photo number and a lock. Numbers are never reused during a run, even after a format, because video_cam remembers every name it has seen (unless restart_numbering_after_format is true).

Sets up the card: resolves the root folder, checks the directory name is a plain folder name (no '..' or slashes, else ValueError), creates the folder, deletes old photos when clear_on_start is true (the default: a fresh card each run), and continues numbering after the highest IMG number still on disk.
Property: the full path of the photo directory (<root>/101SIYI_IMG).
What the media API's getdirectories call answers: always exactly one entry, [{name: '101SIYI_IMG', path: '101SIYI_IMG'}].
True when a path from a getmedialist request means our photo directory; slashes at either end are ignored, so '101SIYI_IMG' and '/101SIYI_IMG/' both match.
Looks through the photo folder for IMG_NNNN.jpg and IMG_NNNN.json files and returns the highest NNNN (0 if none), so numbering can continue after it.

Lists every IMG_NNNN.jpg in the photo folder as PhotoFile records sorted OLDEST FIRST by number. The order matters: video_cam walks the list from the end to find the newest photo. Files that vanish while listing are skipped; the .json sidecars are not listed.
Returns how many photos are on the card (for getmediacount and the status).

Safely maps a URL path like '101SIYI_IMG/IMG_0001.jpg' to a file inside the card. Anything that tries to leave the card (like '../../etc/passwd'), empty parts or missing files give None, so the web server can answer 404.
Tells the name the next photo will get, e.g. 'IMG_0008.jpg', without reserving it.

Stores one photo under the next free IMG_NNNN.jpg name. If a metadata dict is given it is first saved as IMG_NNNN.json (with 'file' and 'index' added); then the JPEG is written. Both use _atomic_write, so the media server never lists or serves a half-written file. Returns the new PhotoFile.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: once per photo, by SiyiEmulator._process_job
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.effects: writes IMG_NNNN.jpg (+ IMG_NNNN.json) into the card folder

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Deletes every file and sub-folder inside the photo directory (keeping the directory) and returns how many entries went; errors on single files are skipped. Callers hold the lock or are still starting up.
Command 0x48 (format SD card): deletes every file in the photo directory under the lock and returns the count. Numbering restarts at IMG_0001 only when restart_numbering_after_format is true.
Helper for json.dumps so the sidecar can contain numpy numbers and arrays: uses .tolist() or .item() when the object has them, otherwise its text.

Writes bytes to a file safely: first into a hidden temp file '.tmp_...' in the same folder, makes it readable (mode 644), then renames it over the target in one step. If anything fails the temp file is removed and the error is raised again.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: A tiny SIYI camera client (SDK over UDP 37260 + media web API over HTTP 82), standard library only, for tests and for poking a camera by hand. It works against the emulator AND a real SIYI camera, so students can check what the hardware really answers. It is also the 'siyi_client' command, for example 'ros2 run siyi_emulator siyi_client hwid', 'angles 30 -45' or 'photo --out p.jpg'.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: Not used during a normal simulated flight (there the team's video_cam is the client). The package's tests and e2e checks use SiyiClient to drive the emulator over real sockets, and AGENTS.md lists 'siyi_client hwid|angles 30 -45|photo --out /tmp/p.jpg' as the hand tool. Nothing outside siyi_emulator imports it (simulation/scripts/take_photo.sh --direct uses sim_bringup's photo_trigger instead).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: A minimal SIYI SDK client: it knows the camera address (default 192.168.144.25), the SDK port 37260, the media port 82 and a reply timeout (2.0 s like video_cam), owns one UDP socket and a sequence counter, and keeps frames that arrived while waiting for something else in 'unsolicited'.
Stores the address, ports and timeout and opens the UDP socket.
Closes the UDP socket.
Lets the client be used in a 'with' block; returns itself.
Closes the socket when the 'with' block ends.
Sends one SDK frame to the camera with CTRL 0x01 ('please answer') or 0x00, using and advancing its own sequence number unless one is given.
Waits (up to the timeout) for a frame whose command number is in the expected set and returns it; other frames that arrive meanwhile are kept in 'unsolicited'. Returns None on timeout.
Sends a command and waits for its reply (by default a reply with the same command number). Returns the reply frame or None after the timeout.
Asks 0x02 and returns the hardware ID text ('6B...' = ZR10, '73...' = A8 mini), or None.
Asks 0x01 and returns the firmware versions as texts like ('v0.3.4', 'v0.3.9', ...), or None.
Asks 0x0A and returns a dict with hdr, record_sta (2 = no SD card), mode (0 lock, 1 follow, 2 fpv), mounting, video_output and the reply length, or None.
Asks 0x0D and returns {yaw, pitch, roll, yaw_rate, pitch_rate, roll_rate} in degrees and deg/s, or None.
Sends 0x0E with a yaw (+ = left) and pitch (-90 = down) in degrees and returns the attitude in the reply (the attitude before moving), or None.
Sends 0x41 for one axis ('yaw' or 'pitch') and returns (reply command number, (yaw, pitch, roll)); the A8 mini answers with command 0x0E, the ZR10 with 0x41. None on timeout.
True when a reply came and its first data byte is 1 (or it has no data): the SDK's 'OK' answer.
Sends 0x07 gimbal speeds -100..100 (yaw + = right, pitch + = up); 0, 0 stops. Returns True on an OK reply.
Sends 0x08: position 1 = centre straight ahead, 2 = centre looking down. Returns True on an OK reply.
Sends 0x0F to zoom to a factor (packed as whole part + tenths). Returns True on an OK reply.
Asks 0x18 and returns the current zoom, or None (a real A8 mini never answers this).
Asks 0x16 and returns the maximum zoom, or None.
Sends 0x05 (1 zoom in, -1 out, 0 stop) and returns the zoom from the reply, or None.
Sends 0x04 auto focus at a video pixel (default 960, 540). Returns True on an OK reply (the emulator says OK unless strict).
Sends 0x06 manual focus (1 far, -1 near, 0 stop). Returns True on an OK reply.
Asks 0x19 and returns 'lock', 'follow' or 'fpv', or None.
Sends 0x0C with function 3/4/5 to switch the gimbal to lock/follow/fpv (never answered).

Takes a photo the way video_cam does: by default it sends video_cam's exact fixed packet 55 66 01 01 00 00 00 0c 00 34 ce (sequence 0 every time), then waits up to 0.8 s for the 0x0B push. Returns its info_type (0 = photo OK, 1 = failed) or None.
Sends 0x48 (format SD card, never answered): deletes every photo. Never use on a real camera you care about.
Property: 'http://<ip>:<media_port>', the base of the media API.
GETs /cgi-bin/media.cgi/api/v1/<api>?<params> from the camera (10 s timeout) and returns the decoded JSON.
Calls getdirectories and returns the list of {name, path} (empty if the call failed).
Calls getmedialist for a folder (default: the LAST folder, like video_cam) and returns the list of {name, url, size}.
Downloads a photo by its listing URL (the host part is replaced by this client's ip and port) or by its file name (looked up in the last folder) and returns the bytes.
Does what video_cam does for one capture: notes the current file names, takes a photo, then polls the listing every 0.25 s (up to 15 s) until a new file appears and downloads it.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.outputs: (0x0B info_type or None, the new listing entry or None, the JPEG bytes or empty)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Prints dicts and lists as indented JSON and anything else as plain text (command-line output).
