The 'siyi_client' command line: options --ip (default 192.168.144.25), --port 37260, --media-port 82, --timeout 2.0 and one sub-command: hwid, firmware, info, attitude, zoom-current, zoom-range, list, dirs, angles YAW PITCH, axis yaw|pitch ANGLE, rotate Y P [--seconds S], center [POS], zoom X (prints the zoom 3 s later), zoom-manual in|out|stop, mode [lock|follow|fpv], photo [--out FILE], download NAME --out FILE, format --yes. Returns 1 when 'photo' got no picture or 'format' lacks --yes.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: ros2 run siyi_emulator siyi_client ...

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: The SIYI camera's 'language' written as code. It builds and reads SIYI SDK packets (called frames): start bytes 55 66, a CTRL byte, the data length, a sequence number, the command number, the data, and a CRC-16/XMODEM checksum at the end. It also packs and unpacks the values inside them: angles in tenths of a degree, zoom as (whole part, tenths) and the 12-byte attitude. Standard-library Python only, no ROS.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: command_handler.py and emulator.py use it to understand what the team's video_cam driver sends to UDP port 37260 and to answer it; sdk_client.py (the siyi_client tool) uses it to talk to a camera. Its frames are bit-exact with video_cam's own: the tests rebuild video_cam's shutter packet 55 66 01 01 00 00 00 0c 00 34 ce.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: The error raised when some bytes are not a valid SIYI frame: too short, wrong start bytes, cut off, an impossible length or a wrong checksum. split_frames catches it, so one bad packet can never crash the emulator.

Computes the 2-byte checksum (CRC-16/XMODEM: polynomial 0x1021, start value 0) that ends every SIYI frame. It simply calls Python's binascii.crc_hqx(data, 0), the same call the team's video_cam driver uses, so both sides always get the same number.

One SIYI SDK packet kept as a read-only record with four fields: cmd_id (the command number, e.g. 0x0E = set gimbal angles), data (the payload bytes), seq (a counter 0..65535; video_cam uses 0 for every photo) and ctrl (bit 0 = 'please answer', bit 1 = 'this is an answer').
Property: True when the sender asked for an answer, i.e. bit 0 (value 0x01) of the CTRL byte is set.
Property: True when this frame is itself an answer, i.e. bit 1 (value 0x02) of the CTRL byte is set. The emulator's replies always use CTRL 0x02.
Property: the readable name of the frame's command, e.g. 'set gimbal angles' for 0x0E (it asks command_name).
Turns the frame back into the exact bytes to send over UDP (header + data + CRC) by calling build_frame with its four fields.
Looks up a readable name for a command number in the COMMAND_NAMES table, e.g. 0x18 -> 'current zoom'. Numbers not in the table give 'unknown command 0xNN'. Used only for log messages.

Builds one complete SIYI frame: 55 66, the CTRL byte, the data length and the sequence number (each 2 bytes, little-endian), the command number, the data, and finally the CRC-16 of everything before it. A payload longer than 65535 bytes raises ValueError. Example: command 0x0C with data 00 and seq 0 gives video_cam's shutter packet 55 66 01 01 00 00 00 0c 00 34 ce.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.inputs: cmd_id 0..255, data bytes, seq (wrapped to 0..65535), ctrl (0x01 request wanting an answer, 0x02 answer, 0x00 no answer wanted)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Reads one frame that starts at the first byte of a buffer. It checks there are at least 10 bytes, that they start with 55 66, that the data length is believable (at most 4096), that the whole frame is present and that the checksum matches; then it returns a Frame. Anything wrong raises FrameError with a short reason; extra bytes after the frame are ignored.

Says how many bytes the frame starting at a given position will take (8 header bytes + its data length + 2 checksum bytes), read from its header. Returns None when fewer than 8 header bytes have arrived yet.

Pulls every valid frame out of one UDP datagram. It skips junk until the next 55 66, accepts several frames sent back to back, and after a broken frame moves one byte forward and tries again, so it never raises. It returns the good frames in order plus a list of short problem texts that the emulator turns into one-time warnings.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.called_when: every time a UDP packet reaches the emulator's SDK port (SiyiEmulator._udp_loop)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Like split_frames, but only hands out the good frames one by one and throws the problem list away.
Converts degrees (or degrees per second) into the protocol's whole-number tenths, e.g. 60.5 -> 605. The result is rounded and kept inside the 16-bit range -32768..32767.
Converts the protocol's tenths back into degrees, e.g. 605 -> 60.5.
Packs the 12-byte answer to command 0x0D (gimbal attitude): yaw, pitch, roll, then their three turning rates, each a little-endian 16-bit number in tenths of a degree (or degrees per second).
Unpacks a 12-byte 0x0D attitude payload back into (yaw, pitch, roll, yaw_rate, pitch_rate, roll_rate) in degrees. Fewer than 12 bytes raises FrameError. Used by the siyi_client tool.
Packs the 6-byte answer to 0x0E (set angles) and 0x41 (single axis): the gimbal's current yaw, pitch and roll in tenths of a degree.
Unpacks a 6-byte angles payload into (yaw, pitch, roll) in degrees. Fewer than 6 bytes raises FrameError.
Packs the 4-byte 0x0E request a client sends: the target yaw and pitch in tenths of a degree. This is what video_cam sends for its gimbal_set_angles command (0,-90 = look straight down).
Reads a 0x0E request payload into (yaw_deg, pitch_deg). Fewer than 4 bytes raises FrameError.
Reads a 0x41 single-axis request (3 bytes: a 16-bit angle in tenths, then an axis byte 0 = yaw, 1 = pitch) into (angle_deg, axis). Fewer than 3 bytes raises FrameError.
Reads a 0x07 gimbal-speed request (two signed bytes) into (turn_yaw, turn_pitch), each kept inside -100..100.

Splits a zoom factor into the protocol's two bytes (whole part, tenths digit). It rounds to the nearest tenth first, so 4.95 becomes (5, 0) and never (4, 10); negative zoom counts as 0 and the whole part is capped at 255.
Joins (whole part, tenths digit) back into one zoom factor, e.g. (4, 5) -> 4.5.
Packs a zoom factor as the 2-byte answer of 0x16 (maximum zoom) and 0x18 (current zoom): whole part, then tenths.
Reads a 2-byte zoom payload back into a zoom factor. The same layout is used by the 0x0F absolute-zoom request, so the command handler uses it for that too. Fewer than 2 bytes raises FrameError.
Packs the answer to 0x05 (manual zoom): the zoom times ten as an unsigned 16-bit number, e.g. 4.5x -> 45, kept inside 0..65535.
Reads a 0x05 answer (unsigned 16-bit zoom x 10) back into a zoom factor, e.g. 45 -> 4.5. Fewer than 2 bytes raises FrameError.
Builds one 32-bit firmware version number the way SIYI sends it: a high byte (0x6E by default, which readers ignore), then major, minor and patch, e.g. 0x6E030203 means version 3.2.3.
Turns bytes into spaced hex text like '55 66 01 ...' for log messages.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: Shared pytest helpers for the emulator tests: synthetic_rgb (a test frame with a white square in the middle), FakeGzLink (pretends to be Gazebo: answers each photo trigger with that frame after a chosen delay, records gimbal targets and echoes them back as measured joints, can inject drone odometry) and the start_emulator fixture, which starts a real SiyiEmulator on 127.0.0.1 with free ports and a temporary SD card. It leaves out test_video_cam_compat.py when video_cam is not built.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Makes a fake camera frame for tests: random dark texture (fixed seed 3) with a white 40x40 square in the middle, so a test can see whether digital zoom made the square bigger.

Test stand-in for GzLink (builds on NullGzLink) that behaves like Gazebo without Gazebo: it answers each photo trigger with the synthetic frame after a chosen delay (or never, to test lost frames), records every gimbal joint target and zoom command, echoes the targets back as 'measured' joint states, and can inject drone odometry.

Sets up the fake as available ('fake gazebo'), with the frame size (2560x1440 by default), the frame delay (0.05 s), whether frames are sent at all, empty records, a pretend sim clock starting at 1.0 s and the synthetic frame.
Pretends to connect; always returns True.
Records the (yaw, roll, pitch) targets, advances the pretend sim clock by 0.02 s and, unless echoing is turned off, feeds them straight back to the emulator as measured joint states.
Records an optical zoom command so a test can check what was sent.

Counts the trigger and, if frames are enabled, starts a background thread that delivers one synthetic RGB frame to the emulator's on_photo callback after frame_delay_s (stamped just after the current pretend sim time).
Inner helper run on the background thread: waits frame_delay_s, then hands one RawImage of the synthetic frame to on_photo.
Injects one drone odometry sample (quaternion x, y, z, w and position, default 30 m up) into the emulator, as if Gazebo had published it; used to test stabilisation.

pytest fixture that returns a factory start_emulator(gz=None, **settings): each call starts a real SiyiEmulator on 127.0.0.1 with free ports, a temporary SD card and pitch 0 (unless overridden), and every emulator started is stopped when the test ends.

The factory returned by start_emulator: applies the test's settings over the safe defaults, checks there are no unknown setting names, builds the emulator with the given fake Gazebo (or NullGzLink), starts it and remembers it for clean-up.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: Drives a running emulator attached to the gimbal_stand test world through the SIYI SDK and the media server like video_cam does, and checks with real rendered photos that: yaw 0 sees the red box, +30 turns LEFT to green, -30 right to blue; pitch -90 sees the yellow disc; 0x0D reports the command; a 0x07 speed of +50 for 1 s turns about 45 deg RIGHT; 3x zoom makes the red box 3x wider; lock/follow modes behave; the horizon stays level while the drone rolls and pitches; every photo comes with 0x0B inside 0.8 s as a 2560x1440 JPEG. Saves photos, a contact sheet and report.json; exit code 0 only if all checks pass.

Integration check against the REAL simulated drone (sim_models iris_a8mini) parked facing north in sim_models' test world: the measured gimbal attitude (0x0D) follows each command, yaw 0 looks north at the red pole 60 m away and yaw +30 turns LEFT to the magenta pole, pitch -90 sees only ground, and every photo comes with 0x0B under 0.8 s as a 2560x1440 JPEG. Saves photos, contact sheet and report.json; exit code 0 only if all pass.

Writes the grass-and-dirt ground texture ground.png (1024x1024, multi-scale noise in greens and browns) for the gimbal_stand test world, so the picture does not have to be stored in the repository. Usage: python3 make_ground_texture.py <output.png>.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator/.explain: Builds the 1024x1024 grass-and-dirt ground picture: adds random noise at four scales, mixes green (grass) and brown (dirt) by that noise, adds fine grain, and returns it as a BGR image.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: End-to-end Gazebo test runner: makes the ground texture, starts the gimbal_stand world HEADLESS in its own GZ_PARTITION (siyi_e2e), starts the emulator on the development address 127.0.0.3 (never the real camera address), runs e2e_gazebo_check.py, then stops only the processes it started. OPTICAL_ZOOM=1 adds ardupilot_gazebo's CameraZoomPlugin. Photos, contact sheet, report.json and logs go to the output folder (default /tmp/siyi_e2e).

Runner for e2e_sim_models_check.py: generates the iris_a8mini drone from its xacro (camera zr10, ArduPilot JSON port 9002+10*INSTANCE, INSTANCE 3 so it never collides with a real simulation; no SITL), spawns it HEADLESS in sim_models' test world in GZ_PARTITION siyi_e2e_models, starts the emulator on 127.0.0.3, runs the check and stops only what it started. Skips with exit 0 when sim_models or the ArduPilot Gazebo plugin is missing.

A small Gazebo Harmonic test world (not the real drone): a floating, gravity-free 'drone' named iris with the same 3-axis gimbal, joint names, topics and cameras as the simulation contract (/sim/gimbal/*/cmd_pos, /sim/gimbal/joint_states, /sim/drone/odometry, live camera 1280x720, triggered photo camera 2560x1440 on /sim/camera/photo/trigger), surrounded by coloured targets at known bearings: red box straight ahead, green 30 deg left, blue 30 deg right, yellow disc straight below, white pole for zoom tests.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: Used by test/e2e/run_e2e_gazebo.sh to check gimbal directions, zoom and stabilisation with real rendered photos.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: Unit tests of camera_state.py: the model profiles and hardware IDs video_cam's model detection reads, the zoom machine (travel, manual ramp, limits, 'within 0.6x after 3 s' as video_cam expects), and the 0x01/0x02/0x0A answer bytes (record_sta is 2 only without an SD card).

Unit tests of command_handler.py: the reply of EVERY emulated command (command number, length, values, echoed sequence number, CTRL 0x02), which commands stay silent (0x0C, 0x48, strict-mode 0x04/0x06/0x16/0x18/0x19), the side effects on gimbal, zoom, mode and the photo/format hooks, and that broken or unknown frames never raise.

End-to-end tests of the running emulator over real sockets on 127.0.0.1 with the fake Gazebo: the photo flow exactly as video_cam sees it (0x0C -> 0x0B within 0.8 s -> new file in the listing -> download -> decodable 2K/4K JPEG), slow or missing Gazebo frames and re-sent triggers, 'no TF card', strict silence, garbage datagrams, gimbal joint publishing and stabilisation from odometry, zoom applied to photos, and format.

Unit tests of gimbal_control.py: rotation helpers, the sign rules (+yaw = camera turns LEFT, pitch -90 = straight down, SIYI speed + = RIGHT), limits and slew rate, inverse-kinematics round trips, level-camera stabilisation while the drone tilts, lock/follow/FPV modes, and what 0x0D reports. Most are ported from the first twin prototype.

Tests of media_server.py over real HTTP on 127.0.0.1: the exact JSON shapes video_cam depends on (getdirectories, getmedialist with count=1 and 9999 and 'total', getmediacount), file download, 404s, SIYI's double-slash URL, media_type checks, URLs built from the Host header, and keep-alive with requests.Session.

Tests of the ROS 2 wrapper node.py, run in-process on 127.0.0.1 with free ports and no Gazebo: every EmulatorConfig field is a ROS parameter, '-p initial_pitch_deg:=-90' (an integer) is accepted for a decimal setting, and one photo gives one JSON message on /sim/camera/photo_info plus state messages on /sim/camera/emulator_state. Skipped without rclpy.

Unit tests of photo.py: Gazebo image byte layouts to OpenCV BGR (RGB, BGR, RGBA, grey, padded rows), digital zoom as centre crop + resize, the zoom and field-of-view maths including the CameraZoomPlugin command, JPEG encoding, and the test pattern (decodable and big enough for video_cam's 50 kB minimum).

Unit tests of sd_card.py: IMG_NNNN.jpg naming, oldest-first listing, one folder per run, atomic writes with JSON sidecars, format (0x48) without reusing names, clear-on-start, and that resolve() cannot be tricked into leaving the card folder.

Unit tests of sdk_protocol.py: CRC-16/XMODEM, building and parsing frames (video_cam's shutter and set-angles packets reproduced bit-exactly, plus SIYI's own example frames), tolerant splitting of datagrams, and every payload encoder/decoder.

Runs last year's REAL camera code (video_cam's CameraInterface and PipelineOrchestrator, unchanged) against the emulator on 127.0.0.1, method by method: model detection, SD card check, the whole capture -> find -> download -> verify -> save pipeline for 2K and 4K, every gimbal/zoom/focus/mode/format call, and the strict A8-mini silences. Skipped when video_cam is not importable.

pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.explain: The tests of siyi_emulator (AGENTS.md lists 147 passing; run 'python3 -m pytest -q test --ignore=test/e2e' or scripts/run_tests.sh). There are unit tests of every module (sdk_protocol, command_handler, camera_state, gimbal_control, photo, sd_card, media_server, node), loopback tests that drive the running emulator over real UDP and HTTP sockets on 127.0.0.1 with a fake Gazebo (conftest.py's FakeGzLink), and test_video_cam_compat.py, which runs the team's real video_cam code against the emulator. The e2e/ folder holds heavier checks that need Gazebo: run_e2e_gazebo.sh with the gimbal_stand test world from fixtures/, and run_e2e_sim_models.sh with the real iris_a8mini drone.
pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/siyi_emulator.how_it_fits: Nothing here runs during a simulated flight: the tests prove the emulator answers like the real SIYI camera, so the team's unchanged video_cam can talk to it.

pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/t.explain: The tests of the plug-and-play part (AGENTS.md lists 219 passing): unit tests of every sim_plugins module (profiles and schema, plan, autopilot, params, contracts, check_slot with a FakeGraph, siyi_probe, launch_support, tracker_filter on the real tracker.launch.xml, profile_tool, doc_blocks), tests of the small hooks inside sim_bringup, an evaluation of sim.launch.py and team_stack.launch.py with a fake launch context, and fetch_sitl.sh tested without the internet. conftest.py puts the SOURCE folders of sim_plugins and sim_bringup on the Python path, so no build is needed. run_tests.sh runs all of it plus profile validation, shellcheck and the demo.sh / start_sim.sh --dry-run comparison, with no Gazebo, SITL or ROS node started.
pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/t.how_it_fits: Run with 'python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider test' (repo layout and ROS sourced) or 'bash test/run_tests.sh' from the package folder; nothing here runs in a simulation.

pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.explain: The tests of the template detector: test_blob_logic.py checks blob_logic.py without ROS (which file names count as finished photos, the GPS position read from a '<lat> , <lon>.jpg' name, and that colour blobs come back as person/tent boxes in FULL-photo pixels with sane scores).
pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.how_it_fits: Run with 'python3 -m pytest -q test' from the example_detector folder; copy and adapt them when you make your own detector from this template.

pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.explain: The tests of the template listener: test_summary.py checks summary.py without ROS (the haversine distance, armed time, modes, distance flown, best detection per class and the JSON summary).
pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugin_ex.how_it_fits: Run with 'python3 -m pytest -q test' from the example_listener folder; copy and adapt them when you make your own extra from this template.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: Checks ANOTHER COPY of the team's Jetson code (a teammate's fork, another branch, this year's code) before the simulator runs it, so a checkout that cannot work stops the demo at once with a clear message instead of a long wait for nodes that never come. It checks that the folder exists and has no space in its path, that its launcher.sh reads TRACKER_CMD and FCU_URL, that ros2_ws is built with the 8 team packages (main, video_cam, detection, mapping, waypoint_mavros, gps_ros2, wp_sender, interfaces) and has main/launch/tracker.launch.xml, and it warns when the node names stack_check waits for or the status texts the phase monitor parses are missing from the sources. Pure Python, no ROS.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: plan.check_environment calls check() when a profile sets run.team_repo (demo.sh --team-repo) and run.team_stack is local, so 'profile_tool plan --check' and 'profile_tool shell' report a broken checkout before ./launcher.sh sim starts it. contracts.TEAM_STACK and 'check_slot --slot team_stack' check the same code once it runs. New on 2026-10-31 (not committed yet).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Reads a text file (UTF-8, bad bytes replaced) and returns its text, or '' when it cannot be read.

Returns all the Python source of one team package (every .py under ros2_ws/src/<package>, skipping files whose path contains '.bak', 'old_' or 'test') joined into one text, or '' when the package folder is missing.

Checks one checkout of the team code and returns (errors, warnings, notes); an empty path gives three empty lists. Errors, each with why and the exact fix: a space in the path, a missing folder, no launcher.sh, a launcher.sh that does not mention TRACKER_CMD or FCU_URL, ros2_ws not built (no install/setup.bash) or missing team packages, no main/launch/tracker.launch.xml. Warnings: a node name from NODE_OF_PACKAGE (waypoint_manager, gps_mavros_service_node, new_od, siyi, mission_camera_trigger, main_controller) or a status text from STATUS_TEXTS not found in its package's source; the note says where the team code comes from.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: by plan.check_environment when the profile sets run.team_repo (and run.team_stack is local)

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: Checks a DETECTOR MODEL FILE (the YOLO weights the team's new_od loads) before a flight, so a wrong file stops the demo in seconds instead of after minutes of flying with a detector that never loaded. quick_check (no ROS, no PyTorch) checks the file exists, is not empty and has no space in its path, its format from the extension (.pt PyTorch, .engine TensorRT, .onnx), that a .pt really starts like PyTorch weights, warns about a same-name .engine next to a .pt, and records size and SHA-256 fingerprint; load_check (PyTorch + Ultralytics) loads it once, times one 640 px tile and checks its class names against the team's class map. Command line: python3 -m sim_plugins.model_check FILE [--load] [--device auto|cpu|cuda:0] [--camera zr10|a8mini] [--no-hash] [--json OUT]; exit 0 = usable, 3 = not usable (EXIT_UNUSABLE, so a script can tell a bad model from a Python that could not even start), 2 = bad usage.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: plan.check_environment runs quick_check without the fingerprint on the team detector's weights (profile_tool plan --check / shell). demo.sh runs 'python3 -m sim_plugins.model_check --no-hash <weights>' for the real detector and counts exit 3 as a problem that stops the start, and run_meta.detector_meta runs check() (with --load in demo.sh) just before the flight for run_meta/detector.json. setup.py installs it as the console script model_check. TEAM_CLASS_MAP copies detection/detection_processor.py's CLASS_MAP (person, mannequin, doll -> person; umbrella, kite -> tent); new on 2026-10-31 (not committed yet).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Everything known about one model file: the expanded path, the file name, the format (pytorch, tensorrt, onnx or unknown), the size in bytes, the SHA-256 fingerprint, lists of errors (each says what, why and the fix), warnings and notes, and load_check's results (empty when it did not run).
Property: True when the report has no errors (warnings are allowed).
Returns the report as a JSON-ready dict, adding 'ok' and the size in MB ('size_mb', one decimal).

Returns printable lines in the style of the other tools: ' OK model <name>: <format>, <MB> MB, sha256 <first 16 hex digits>...' when the size is known, then ' .. ' notes, ' !! ' warnings and ' XX ' errors.
Expands '~' and $VARIABLES in a path text and trims spaces at both ends.
Computes a file's SHA-256 fingerprint, reading it in 1 MB pieces, and returns it as hex text (a 40 MB model takes well under a second).
True when a Python module (for example tensorrt or onnxruntime) could be imported here, found with importlib.util.find_spec without importing it (so no slow PyTorch start).
Returns the first few bytes of a file (8 by default), or empty bytes when it cannot be read.
True when a file starts like PyTorch weights: a zip archive (bytes 'PK' 03 04, torch 1.6 and newer) or a pickle (first byte 0x80, older files).

The fast checks, which never raise: no path, a space in the path, a missing, empty or unreadable file are errors, and the extension decides the format (anything but .pt, .engine and .onnx is refused). A .pt that does not start like PyTorch weights (for example a saved web page) is an error and a same-name .engine next to it a warning (new_od would load the .engine first); a .engine without the tensorrt module is an error, or only a warning when a .pt twin sits next to it; an .onnx needs onnxruntime. It also stores the size and, unless compute_hash is false, the SHA-256 fingerprint.
Counts how many 640 px tiles (15 % overlap) new_od's SAHI path cuts a photo into, plus one full-photo pass: for a 2560 x 1440 photo that is 5 x 3 + 1 = 16.
Inner helper: the number of tiles along one side of the photo: 1 when the side fits in one tile, else ceil((size - tile) / step) + 1 with step = tile x (1 - overlap).

Sorts a model's class names (lower-cased) into those the team code turns into a person (person, mannequin, doll), those it turns into a tent (umbrella, kite), and 'tent'-like names the team's class map does not know and would therefore ignore.

Turns class_coverage into (warnings, notes): a warning when no class becomes a person or no class becomes a tent (then nothing is dropped on it), a warning for tent-like classes the team code ignores (fix: call the class 'umbrella', or change the team's CLASS_MAP), and a note listing the classes the team code uses.

Loads the model once with Ultralytics YOLO like new_od (on cuda:0 when CUDA works, else the CPU, or the device asked for), runs one warm-up and three timed predictions on an empty 640 x 640 tile, and adds the load time, class names, milliseconds per tile, and tiles and seconds per photo for the camera's photo size to the report. Missing PyTorch/Ultralytics or a model that does not load becomes an error with a fix; running on the CPU, or more than 3 s per photo on the GPU, becomes a warning (the camera takes 1 photo per second and main_controller waits at most 90 s); then it adds the class findings. It does nothing when the quick check already found errors, and never raises.
Runs quick_check (with the SHA-256 fingerprint unless compute_hash is false) and, when load is true, load_check (which does nothing if errors were already found), and returns the report.

Defines the options: the model file, --load, --device (auto, cpu, cuda:0), --camera (a8mini or zr10, for the per-photo estimate), --no-hash (skip the SHA-256 fingerprint for a quick look) and --json OUT.

Command line: checks the model (with the fingerprint unless --no-hash, and loads it with --load), prints the report, writes it as JSON with --json (a write error is only warned about), prints an ERROR line when the model cannot be used, and returns 0 when it is usable, else 3 (EXIT_UNUSABLE).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: python3 -m sim_plugins.model_check FILE [--load] [--device ...] [--camera ...] [--no-hash] [--json OUT] (demo.sh: --no-hash on the team detector's weights), or the model_check console script

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/t.explain: Keeps the repo's documentation findable: it runs the docs checker simulation/scripts/check_docs.py on the real repo (every Markdown file must be listed in the index docs/README.md; links in the index and relative links inside any doc must point to files or #sections that exist; scripts a doc names under simulation/scripts/, simulation/jetson/, setup/, docker/ or windows/ must exist). It also tests the checker itself on small pretend repos in a temporary folder: each rule fails when it should, a planned doc or script under '## Being written' does not, links in code, comments and web links are not checked, allow-listed and gitignored files need no index line, and heading anchors follow GitHub's rules.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/t.how_it_fits: pytest suite of sim_plugins (standard library + pytest, no ROS), next to test_doc_blocks.py; NEW on 2026-10-31 (10:30).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: Writes down WHICH PIECES REALLY RAN in a simulator run, as three small JSON files: run_meta/autopilot.json (the ArduCopter version the autopilot itself reported, from its boot banner such as 'ArduCopter V4.6.3 (3fc7011a)' in sim.log or from the MAVLink message AUTOPILOT_VERSION, plus the program file with its SHA-256 and the --defaults parameter files read from the running SITL process), run_meta/detector.json (kind real/team/truth/custom; for the team's new_od the weights file with size, SHA-256, format and model_check's verdict) and run_meta/team_stack.json (the checkout folder, its git commit, launcher.sh's SHA-256, TRACKER_CMD and FCU_URL). Every file has 'schema': 'astra.run_meta.<what>.v1' and a 'written' time, and the format only ever grows by new keys. Usage: python3 -m sim_plugins.run_meta autopilot|detector|team-stack --out FILE plus the options of that record; setup.py also installs it as the console script run_meta. Exit code 0 = written, 3 = the detector model cannot be used (the file is still written), 1 = the file could not be written, 2 = bad usage.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: demo.sh calls it three times per run (added 10:52 on 2026-10-31): first 'run_meta detector --kind <detector> --model <weights> --camera <model> --text ...' (with --load for the real detector) before anything starts, and it stops the demo on exit 3; then 'run_meta autopilot --sim-log <run>/sim.log --state ~/.astra_sim/state/current_launch.yaml --session $ASTRA_SIM_SESSION --wait 5 --mavlink <ground-station URL> --mavlink-timeout 6' between two mission_tool calls; and 'run_meta team-stack --repo <checkout> --tracker-cmd ... --fcu-url ...' when the team stack runs locally. Any other recorder failure is only a warning, so it never stops a flight. It reuses model_check (check, sha256_of, EXIT_UNUSABLE) and autopilot.read_binary_version, and finds the SITL process in /proc by its '--model JSON' arguments and ASTRA_SIM_SESSION. New on 2026-10-31 (not committed yet).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.effects: writes the JSON file given by --out (folders created); autopilot: reads /proc, sim.log and the state file, and with --mavlink sends one MAVLink request; detector --load: loads the model once; team-stack: runs read-only git commands

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Returns the local time as text, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', for the 'written' key of every record.
Writes one record as JSON indented by 2 spaces plus a final newline, creating the missing folders first.
Describes one file as {path, size_bytes, sha256}, with the SHA-256 from model_check.sha256_of. A missing file gives {path, missing: true} and a read error gives {path, error}.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: for the SITL program, each --defaults parameter file and launcher.sh

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Finds the LAST ArduPilot boot banner in a log text, e.g. 'ArduCopter V4.6.3 (3fc7011a)' (ArduPlane, ArduRover, ArduSub, Blimp and AntennaTracker are matched too). It returns {firmware, version, git, banner}, plus 'frame' when the text also has a 'Frame: ...' line, or None when there is no banner.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.inputs: the text of sim.log (MAVProxy logs the banner as an 'AP:' line)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Unpacks AUTOPILOT_VERSION.flight_sw_version, which packs major<<24 | minor<<16 | patch<<8 | type, into {'version': 'major.minor.patch', 'type': ...}. The type is dev (0), alpha (64), beta (128), rc (192) or official (255); any other number is written as that number.

Turns AUTOPILOT_VERSION.flight_custom_version (8 bytes holding the start of the firmware's git hash as ASCII letters) into text, stopping at the first zero byte. It returns '' when the bytes cannot be read.

Picks the interesting parts out of an arducopter command line: the program (first word), the instance (-I N, -IN or --instance N, turned into a number), --home, the --defaults parameter files (a comma list, also written --defaults=...) and whether -w / --wipe was given.

Looks through /proc for the running ArduPilot SITL: a process whose command line contains '--model' and 'JSON' (that is how sim.launch.py starts it), skipping the wait_then_exec helper that starts it. With a session id, only a process whose environment holds ASTRA_SIM_SESSION=<session> counts, so another person's simulator on the same computer is never picked. Returns {pid, argv, exe} of the first match in /proc's folder order, or None.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.inputs: session id ('' = any), the /proc folder (tests pass a fake one)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Reads the simulator's state file ~/.astra_sim/state/current_launch.yaml (written by sim.launch.py) with PyYAML. It returns {} when the file is missing or broken, or is not a mapping.

Opens a MAVLink connection with pymavlink (as system 254, component 191), waits for a heartbeat, then asks for AUTOPILOT_VERSION (COMMAND_LONG MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE = 512 with message id 148) every 2 s until the timeout (default 8 s). It returns {version, type, git, board_version, source}, or None when pymavlink is missing, nothing answered or anything failed; it never raises and always closes the connection. Its docstring warns to use only an address nobody else is listening on at that moment.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: by autopilot_meta when --mavlink is given
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.effects: opens and closes a MAVLink link; sends MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE to the autopilot

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Builds the autopilot.json record and never raises. It takes kind, sitl_run_dir and profile from the state file, waits up to --wait seconds for the boot banner in sim.log (re-reading the log once a second), and with --mavlink also asks AUTOPILOT_VERSION. It then finds the running SITL process (not for kind external) and records its pid, command line, instance, home, wipe flag and each --defaults file's fingerprint, or else falls back to sitl_bin from the state file, and fingerprints the program with the version compiled into it (autopilot.read_binary_version). Notes say what could not be found, and when the reported version and the compiled version differ.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.outputs: dict: schema astra.run_meta.autopilot.v1, written, kind, reported, binary, process, run_dir, profile, notes (+ autopilot_version with --mavlink)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Builds the detector.json record: schema astra.run_meta.detector.v1, written, kind and the short description text. For kind real or team (the team's new_od) it runs model_check.check on the weights file (loading it once only with --load, on --device, for the --camera photo size) and records the model's name, path, size, SHA-256 and format, plus the check's ok, loaded, errors, warnings, notes and load results.

Returns {commit, branch, dirty} of a git checkout by running 'git rev-parse HEAD', 'git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD' and 'git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no' (10 s limit each). It returns None when the folder has no .git or git cannot run.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.effects: runs read-only git commands in that folder

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Inner helper of git_info: runs one 'git -C <repo> ...' command and returns its standard output with spaces trimmed (a failing git command just gives its empty or partial output).

Builds the team_stack.json record: the checkout folder, launcher.sh's fingerprint (size and SHA-256), the git commit, branch and dirty flag (git_info), and TRACKER_CMD and FCU_URL as given. When the folder is not a git checkout (like the simulator's Linux copy made by simulation/setup/03_build.sh, which has no .git), a note says to look at the Windows checkout for the commit.

Defines the three sub-commands and their options: autopilot (--out, --sim-log, --state, --session, --wait 0, --mavlink, --mavlink-timeout 8), detector (--out, --kind real|team|truth|custom, --model, --text, --load, --device auto, --camera zr10|a8mini) and team-stack (--out, --repo, --tracker-cmd, --fcu-url).

run_meta's command line: runs the chosen sub-command, prints a one-line summary (for a real/team detector the full model_check report), and writes the record with write_json. It returns 3 (model_check.EXIT_UNUSABLE) when the detector model cannot be used (the record is still written), 1 when the file cannot be written, else 0; argparse itself exits with 2 on bad usage.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: by demo.sh three times per run (detector, autopilot, team-stack), or by hand: python3 -m sim_plugins.run_meta ... or the run_meta console script
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.effects: writes the --out JSON file; see the module entry for what each sub-command reads

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: The graph check for the team_stack slot (the whole Jetson code as one piece). Every node name in the contract (mavros, waypoint_manager, gps_mavros_service_node, mission_camera_trigger, siyi, new_od, main_controller) must be running, minus the --skip-node names and plus the --add-node names, like stack_check; each running node is reported ok and the missing ones as one fail with a hint (is ./launcher.sh sim running, see team_stack.log; a renamed node needs a profile with a custom slot). Then it checks the contract's topics and services with any node allowed to provide them (check_topics / check_services with node '').
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: by evaluate for --slot team_stack (evaluate then returns at once: no sample message for this slot)
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.inputs: graph, the team_stack contract, report, skip and add node names

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Says in plain words why one unreadable parameter-file line could not be read, for the error message: no value after the name, a name that is not an ArduPilot parameter name (1-16 capital letters, digits and _), a value that is not a number, a value longer than 32 characters (MAX_VALUE_CHARS), or simply not NAME,VALUE.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: by report_errors, for each bad line it shows

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.explain: Turns the problems of one prepared parameter file that must STOP the start into error texts, each with the fix. Unreadable lines: it shows the first 5 with line number, text and bad_line_reason (then 'and N more') and says to correct, delete or comment them out, or to save the file again from Mission Planner (CONFIG > Full Parameter List > Save to file); a file with no NAME,VALUE lines at all is reported as probably the wrong file. A real Mission Planner or QGroundControl file never has bad lines, so loading such a file anyway would silently lose settings the person expects.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.called_when: by autopilot.plan_autopilot for every extra parameter file; its errors become plan errors, so sim.launch.py stops with 'the autopilot cannot start' and profile_tool plan --check reports them
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/si.outputs: list of error texts ([] = the file is fine)

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.explain: Runs ANOTHER COPY of the team's Jetson code (demo.sh --team-repo DIR, profile key run.team_repo) together with the simulator's launch helpers. That checkout's launcher.sh only knows its own ros2_ws, which has the team packages but not sim_bringup (where team_stack.launch.py lives), so this script sources the simulator's ros2_ws/install/local_setup.bash first and the checkout's LAST, which makes the checkout's main, detection, video_cam, mapping and other team packages win over the simulator's copies. It prints '[team_overlay] <package> comes from <folder>' for main, detection, video_cam, mapping, waypoint_mavros, interfaces and sim_bringup, warns when main does not come from the checkout, and then replaces itself with the given command (exec), or with --show only prints that list. Exit code: the command's own, or 2 for bad usage, a workspace that is not built, or sim_bringup not found.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.how_it_fits: demo.sh wraps the team command in it when --team-repo is given: TRACKER_CMD='bash <simulator repo>/ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/scripts/team_overlay.sh --sim-ws <simulator repo>/ros2_ws --team-ws <checkout>/ros2_ws -- ros2 launch sim_bringup team_stack.launch.py detector:=...', and the checkout's own ./launcher.sh sim then runs that command, like on the Jetson. It is run from the source tree (setup.py does not install it). Nothing is copied or changed in either checkout, and team_stack.log in the run folder shows which copy of each package ran. New on 2026-10-31 (10:50, not committed yet).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/s.effects: sources two ROS workspaces into its own environment and runs 'ros2 pkg prefix'; then becomes the given command (normally ros2 launch sim_bringup team_stack.launch.py, which starts the team nodes)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/sc.explain: Prints '[team_overlay] ERROR: <message>' on standard error and stops the script with exit code 2.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/sc.called_when: for an unknown option, a missing --sim-ws or --team-ws, a workspace without install/local_setup.bash, no command after -- (unless --show), or sim_bringup not found in the simulator's workspace

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/t.explain: Unit tests of the detector model check (model_check.py) without PyTorch, 21 tests: a missing, empty, space-in-path, wrongly named or broken weights file gives an error that says what, why and the fix; an old-pickle .pt is accepted and a web page saved as .pt is refused; a TensorRT .engine without TensorRT is refused, or only warned when a .pt twin sits next to it; --no-hash skips the SHA-256 fingerprint; the tile estimate matches new_od's tiling; the class-name checks warn about a model with no person or tent classes and about a class literally called 'tent'; the copy of the team's class map matches the team file; and the command line exits 0 or 3 and writes --json.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/t.how_it_fits: pytest suite of sim_plugins (standard library + pytest, no ROS, no PyTorch); new on 2026-10-31.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/t.explain: Unit tests of the 'what really ran' recorder (run_meta.py) without a simulator, 11 tests: the last ArduCopter boot banner and frame are read from a real-looking sim.log, AUTOPILOT_VERSION numbers decode, the SITL command line is parsed, and a FAKE /proc process table gives the program, instance, home and --defaults files of this session's SITL only. They also check that a version mismatch and a missing banner are noted, an external autopilot is not looked for, the detector record holds the model's name, size and SHA-256, the team-stack record of a plain folder holds the checkout, and the command line writes every run_meta/*.json, exiting 3 for a bad model while still writing the file.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/t.how_it_fits: pytest suite of sim_plugins (standard library + pytest, no ROS); new on 2026-10-31.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_plugins/t.explain: Unit tests of the check of ANOTHER COPY of the team's Jetson code (team_repo.py, profile key run.team_repo / demo.sh --team-repo), 10 tests: an empty setting checks nothing; a missing folder, a folder with a space, no launcher.sh, an old launcher without TRACKER_CMD / FCU_URL, an unbuilt or half-built ros2_ws and a missing tracker.launch.xml each give an error with the fix; a complete pretend checkout passes; a renamed node is only a warning. One test reads the REAL team sources in this repo and checks that they contain every node name and status text the simulator watches, so team_repo.py's lists cannot drift away from the team code unnoticed.
